<!-- Source: README.md -->

# @codenhub/styles

Build a consistent, themeable interface by writing class names on plain HTML: one stylesheet with tokens, a reset, layout and type helpers, and classes for buttons, form fields, alerts, cards, tables, and tooltips. There is no JavaScript to load and no component library to wrap.

## Installation

```sh
pnpm add @codenhub/styles
```

## Usage

Import the compiled stylesheet, which holds everything the package ships:

```css
@import "@codenhub/styles";
```

```html
<form class="card stack">
  <h2 class="text-title-sm">Profile</h2>
  <div class="field">
    <label class="label" for="display-name">Display name</label>
    <input class="ipt" id="display-name" name="display-name" />
  </div>
  <button class="btn primary" type="submit">Save changes</button>
</form>
```

To use the Tailwind CSS v4 source entrypoints instead, or to load only part of the package, see [Setup](./docs/setup.md). The [demo](https://demo.codenhub.dev/styles/) shows every component in every intent, presentation, and aesthetic.

## Documentation

The docs build one account settings screen from start to finish, in this order:

- [Introduction](./docs/index.md): What the package is for, what it costs, and the reading order.
- [Setup](./docs/setup.md): Install the package, choose compiled CSS or Tailwind source, and render the page shell.
- [Integrating](./docs/integrating/index.md): Load the stylesheet in Next.js, Vue, Svelte, Astro, Tailwind CSS v4, or a page with no bundler.
- [Building a screen](./docs/concepts.md): Lay out the page and learn intent, fill, edge, and aesthetic.
- [Usage](./docs/usage/index.md): Guides for buttons, forms, feedback, tooltips, theming, aesthetics, and solo classes, then the lookup pages for every class, token, and default.
- [Accessibility](./docs/accessibility.md): What the CSS does for your users and what your application still owes them.
- [Changelog](./docs/changelog/index.md): Release history, including breaking changes.

## Requirements

| Requirement   | Details                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| CSS imports   | Consumer tooling must resolve package CSS imports.                                                                                                       |
| Browsers      | Chrome 123, Safari 17.5, or Firefox 128 and newer (`light-dark()` theming; `:has()` for `.input-group` state; `@property` for non-inheriting elevation). |
| Tailwind CSS  | 4.3.2 or newer, below 5, only for the `/tw` source entrypoints. Install it yourself; the package does not.                                               |
| Node.js       | 24 or newer, only on the machine that runs the `chs build` command. The stylesheets need none.                                                           |
| Accessibility | Consumers provide semantic HTML, ARIA, keyboard behavior, and focus management.                                                                          |

## Notes

This package has no JavaScript behavior. It ships no compatibility aliases: a removed class or token is documented in the [changelog](./docs/changelog/index.md), not kept under a second name. Below 1.0 a minor release may break and a patch release never does; see [Versioning](./docs/index.md#versioning).

# @codenhub/styles

`@codenhub/styles` lets you build a consistent, themeable interface by writing class names on plain HTML. You import one stylesheet and get tokens, a reset, layout and type helpers, and classes for buttons, form fields, alerts, cards, tables, and tooltips. There is no JavaScript to load and no component library to wrap: a `<button class="btn primary">` is the whole integration.

These docs build one small screen from start to finish, an account settings page with a profile form, a plan summary, and a danger zone. Each page adds something to it, so by the end you have seen every part of the package working together instead of in isolation.

```html
<main class="section">
  <div class="section-content narrow stack">
    <h1 class="text-title">Account settings</h1>
    <form class="card stack">
      <h2 class="text-title-sm">Profile</h2>
      <div class="field">
        <label class="label" for="display-name">Display name</label>
        <input class="ipt" id="display-name" name="display-name" value="Ada Lovelace" />
      </div>
      <div class="cluster">
        <button class="btn primary" type="submit">Save changes</button>
        <button class="btn ghost" type="reset">Cancel</button>
      </div>
    </form>
  </div>
</main>
```

## Three choices per component

Every component answers three independent questions with classes, so a new look never needs a new component variant:

- **Intent: which color?** `.primary`, `.secondary`, `.success`, `.warning`, `.destructive`, or `.info`. Leave it off for neutral.
- **Presentation: how much of that color?** `.solid`, `.soft`, or `.ghost` sets the fill; `.edged` or `.edgeless` sets the border.
- **Aesthetic: what is it made of?** An optional class such as `.neobrutalism` or `.glass` changes corners, border width, shadows, and type for everything inside it.

`<button class="btn destructive ghost edged">Delete account</button>` is a red outlined button, and wrapping the page in `.pixel` turns it into a pixel-art one without touching the button. [Building a screen](docs/concepts.md) introduces each axis as the settings page needs it.

## Compiled CSS or Tailwind source

The package ships the same classes two ways:

- **Compiled CSS**, ready to use. Import it from any bundler, or link the file from a CDN. You do not need Tailwind.
- **Tailwind CSS v4 source**, under `@codenhub/styles/tw`. Use it when your project already runs Tailwind v4, so your build compiles the package with your own utilities and theme.

[Setup](docs/setup.md) helps you choose.

## What it does not do

- **No JavaScript.** There is no runtime, no framework bindings, and no generated code. Anything that needs a script, such as opening a dialog, toggling a theme, or dismissing a tooltip, is your code.
- **No semantics or behavior.** The classes paint elements; they do not add HTML semantics, ARIA, keyboard handling, focus management, validation, or announcements. [Accessibility](docs/accessibility.md) draws the exact line.
- **No theme switching.** Choosing light or dark is a class or attribute you set. The separate `@codenhub/theme` package can remember and apply the choice for you.
- **No fonts or icons.** No font file is downloaded. Aesthetics that want a special font fall back to a system font until you supply one. Icons, including loading spinners, come from your own icon set, such as `@codenhub/icons`.
- **No compatibility aliases.** A removed class or token is listed in the changelog, not kept under its old name.

## Trade-offs

Know these costs before you adopt it:

- **Class names are short and unprefixed.** `.primary`, `.success`, `.dark`, `.label`, `.field`, `.section`, `.stack`, `.flat`, and `.ghost` are global names. Another stylesheet on the same page that uses them collides with this one. The package sits in [cascade layers](docs/setup.md#cascade-layers), so your own unlayered CSS wins a collision, but a third-party library's rules for the same name still apply alongside the package's.
- **The complete stylesheets are large before compression.** At the time of writing, minified, the complete stylesheet is about 198 KB, `/native` about 295 KB, and `/components` about 159 KB. Served with gzip they are about 17 KB, 22 KB, and 13 KB. Focused files are much smaller: `/theme` is about 12 KB (3 KB with gzip) and one aesthetic is 4 to 14 KB (1 to 2 KB with gzip). Most of the size is composition that every component repeats, which is why compression removes so much of it. A compiled file ships every class, whether a page uses it or not. To ship only the classes your pages use, compile the package in your own build: through [Tailwind CSS v4](docs/integrating/tailwind.md) when the project runs it, or with the package's [`build` command](docs/integrating/without-a-bundler.md#build-only-the-classes-you-use) in any other project. A page with one button gets 26 to 28 KB minified that way, and about 6 KB with gzip. Otherwise import the narrowest entrypoint that covers a page; see [Setup → All entrypoints](docs/setup.md#all-entrypoints).
- **`--color-foreground` is a background, not a text color.** It is the tone one step off the page that a quiet card or panel sits on. The text color is `--color-text`.
- **Four hover colors are fixed values.** `--color-success-hover`, `--color-warning-hover`, `--color-destructive-hover`, and `--color-info-hover` are precomputed, because mixing them live crashed WebKit. If you override `--color-success` alone, its hover keeps the old hue, so replace the whole family; see [Theming → Color tokens](docs/usage/theming.md#color-tokens).
- **Modern browsers only.** Chrome 123, Safari 17.5, or Firefox 128 and newer. There is no fallback layer for older browsers.

## What counts as supported

A combination of classes is supported when these docs describe it and the public demo at [demo.codenhub.dev/styles](https://demo.codenhub.dev/styles/) shows it. The demo renders the package's test fixtures, including the full intent, presentation, and aesthetic matrices, against the built CSS. A combination that is neither documented nor shown may still produce CSS, but it is not maintained and can change in any release.

The demo is rebuilt from the main branch, not from each release. It can show work that has not been released yet, so when the demo and these docs disagree about a released version, the docs and the [changelog](docs/changelog/index.md) for that version win.

## Versioning

The package is below 1.0 and follows the [semantic versioning rule for 0.x releases](https://semver.org/#spec-item-4): the public surface can still change between minor versions.

- A minor release, such as 0.7.0 to 0.8.0, may break. It can rename or remove a class or token, or change a default. Every break is listed under **Changed** or **Removed** on that version's [changelog](docs/changelog/index.md) page, with what to use instead.
- A patch release, such as 0.7.0 to 0.7.1, never breaks.

npm's default range for a new dependency, `^0.9.0`, already accepts patches only, because below 1.0 a caret range does not cross into the next minor version. Read the changelog before raising it. When you link a file from a CDN, put the exact version in the URL; see [Without a bundler](docs/integrating/without-a-bundler.md).

Breaks are not softened with aliases because the model is still settling, and keeping each old name beside its replacement would grow the surface every release. A rename or removal usually costs one find-and-replace when you upgrade; a changed default may need your own CSS retuned.

## Reading path

Read these in order the first time. Each page adds to the settings screen and ends by pointing to the next one.

1. [Setup](docs/setup.md): install the package, choose compiled CSS or Tailwind source, and render the empty page shell.
2. [Integrating](docs/integrating/index.md): only if you use Next.js, Vue, Svelte, Astro, Tailwind v4, or no bundler at all. Each guide returns you to the main path.
3. [Building a screen](docs/concepts.md): lay out the page, set its type, and add a card and a Save button, learning intent, fill, and edge on the way.
4. [Usage](docs/usage/index.md): the rest of the screen, in order:
   - [Buttons](docs/usage/buttons.md): secondary and destructive actions, sizes, icon buttons, and disabled states.
   - [Forms](docs/usage/forms.md): labeled fields, hints, errors, icons, selects, checkboxes, radios, and switches.
   - [Feedback](docs/usage/feedback.md): a saving state, a success alert, a plan badge, a loading placeholder, and a usage bar.
   - [Tooltips](docs/usage/tooltips.md): field help that works with a mouse, a keyboard, and a screen reader.
   - [Theming](docs/usage/theming.md): light and dark mode, brand colors, and your own intents.
   - [Aesthetics](docs/usage/aesthetics.md): restyle the whole screen with one class.
   - [Solo classes](docs/usage/solo.md): paint an aesthetic onto a component this package does not style.
   - [Composing](docs/usage/composing.md), [Customizing](docs/usage/customizing.md), and [Content and layout](docs/usage/content-and-layout.md): lookup pages with every axis rule, token, default, and helper class.
   - [Presets](docs/usage/presets.md): set a look once, for a region, a theme, or your own component class, instead of repeating it on every element.
5. [Accessibility](docs/accessibility.md): what the CSS handles for you and what your application must still do.

The [changelog](docs/changelog/index.md) lists every release and what changed in it.

<!-- Source: docs/setup.md -->

# Setup

This page gets the stylesheet into your project and puts the empty shell of the settings screen on the page. It takes one install, one import, and one choice: compiled CSS or Tailwind source. The rest of the page is reference you can come back to: every entrypoint, the classless option, the cascade layers, and what goes wrong when an import is missing.

## Install

```sh
pnpm add @codenhub/styles
```

`npm install @codenhub/styles` and `yarn add @codenhub/styles` work the same way.

## Import the stylesheet

Import the complete compiled stylesheet once, in the CSS file your app already loads globally:

```css
@import "@codenhub/styles";
```

Then write the shell of the settings screen. It is a page section with a centered, narrow column:

```html
<main class="section">
  <div class="section-content narrow stack">
    <h1 class="text-title">Account settings</h1>
    <p>Manage your profile, plan, and security.</p>
  </div>
</main>
```

If the heading renders in a bold, tight title face with the paragraph spaced below it, and the column sits in the middle of a wide window, the stylesheet is working. If it looks like unstyled browser defaults, see [When nothing is styled](#when-nothing-is-styled).

The complete stylesheet includes the reset, the tokens, the layout and type helpers, and every component class. It applies global rules to your page: the reset, the root theme, and focus rings. It does not include the aesthetics or the classless element mappings; both are separate imports, described below.

## Choose your route

Pick one:

- **Compiled CSS** (`@codenhub/styles`, shown above). Use it unless you have a reason not to. Any bundler that resolves CSS imports from packages works, such as Vite, webpack, or the Tailwind CLI. It ships every class, whether your pages use it or not.
- **Tailwind CSS v4 source** (`@codenhub/styles/tw`). Use it when your project already runs Tailwind v4. Your build compiles the package with your own utilities, so you get one stylesheet and Tailwind's `dark:` variant matches the package's theme. It needs Tailwind 4.3.2 or newer, below 5.
- **No bundler.** Link the compiled file from `node_modules` or a CDN with a `<link>` tag; see [Without a bundler](docs/integrating/without-a-bundler.md).

To ship only the classes your pages use in a project that does not run Tailwind, with a bundler or without one, the package's `chs build` command reads your files and writes a stylesheet with only those classes, which you import or link in place of the compiled one; see [Build only the classes you use](docs/integrating/without-a-bundler.md#build-only-the-classes-you-use).

Your framework may need its own wiring, such as where the global stylesheet goes in Next.js or Astro. Each of these guides covers one setup and then sends you back here:

- [Tailwind CSS v4](docs/integrating/tailwind.md)
- [Next.js](docs/integrating/nextjs.md)
- [Vue](docs/integrating/vue.md)
- [Svelte](docs/integrating/svelte.md)
- [Astro](docs/integrating/astro.md)
- [Without a bundler](docs/integrating/without-a-bundler.md)

## Add an aesthetic (optional)

Aesthetics are separate stylesheets because most pages use one or none. Import all six at once, or only the one you use:

```css
@import "@codenhub/styles";
@import "@codenhub/styles/aesthetics/neobrutalism";
```

The order of the two imports does not matter, because every entrypoint declares the [cascade layers](#cascade-layers) before using one. [Aesthetics](docs/usage/aesthetics.md) shows what each one does; you can skip them until then.

## Requirements

- **Browsers:** Chrome 123, Safari 17.5, or Firefox 128 and newer. Colors use `light-dark()` and `color-scheme` (Firefox 120). `.input-group` reads a nested control's invalid and disabled state with `:has()` (Firefox 121). The elevation classes register a non-inheriting property with `@property` (Firefox 128); without it, an elevation class would also reach the unclassed elements inside it.
- **Tooling:** an `@import` of a package name needs a tool that resolves CSS imports from packages through their `exports` map. Without one, link the compiled file by its path or from a CDN; see [Without a bundler](docs/integrating/without-a-bundler.md). Two common tools need a nudge, described in [Integrating → Bundlers that need a nudge](docs/integrating/index.md#bundlers-that-need-a-nudge): Parcel, and PostCSS with `postcss-import`.
- **Tailwind:** 4.3.2 or newer, below 5, only for the `/tw` source entrypoints. It is an optional peer dependency, so the compiled entrypoints and the `chs build` command do not install it.
- **Node.js:** 24 or newer, only on the machine that runs the `chs build` command. The stylesheets need none.
- **Your application:** the package has no JavaScript. Semantic HTML, ARIA, keyboard behavior, focus management, validation, and announcements are yours; see [Accessibility](docs/accessibility.md).

## When nothing is styled

- **The import is missing or not loaded globally.** The classes do nothing until the stylesheet is on the page. Import it once in a stylesheet every page loads, not in a component that may not render.
- **The package name does not resolve.** A plain `<link>` or a tool without CSS package resolution cannot read `@import "@codenhub/styles"`. Link `node_modules/@codenhub/styles/dist/index.css`, or follow [Without a bundler](docs/integrating/without-a-bundler.md). Parcel and `postcss-import` resolve it with a small change; see [Integrating → Bundlers that need a nudge](docs/integrating/index.md#bundlers-that-need-a-nudge).
- **A `/tw` path is loaded without Tailwind.** The `/tw` files are Tailwind source: they contain `@theme`, `@utility`, and `@apply`, which browsers do not understand. Your Tailwind build has to compile them; see [Tailwind CSS v4](docs/integrating/tailwind.md).
- **A focused `/tw` entrypoint is imported without Tailwind before it.** `@codenhub/styles/tw/button` and the other focused component files do not import Tailwind themselves. Imported alone, they compile without an error but produce no component rules. Put `@import "tailwindcss";` before them; see [Tailwind CSS v4 → Using a focused entrypoint](docs/integrating/tailwind.md#using-a-focused-entrypoint).
- **A class built at runtime is missing (Tailwind source only).** Tailwind generates a utility class, the package's components such as `.btn` included, only when it finds the name in your source files. A name assembled from strings, such as `` `btn ${tone}` ``, is invisible to that scan. Write full class names, or list them as described in [Tailwind CSS v4](docs/integrating/tailwind.md).

### Inlining critical CSS

You can paste a **compiled** stylesheet, from `dist/` or from your own build output, into an HTML `<style>` element, for example to inline critical CSS in a server-rendered head. None of the compiled files contains the `</style` sequence that would end the element early.

That does not apply to the `/tw` files. They are Tailwind source, not finished CSS, so pasting one into `<style>` gives the browser directives it ignores and the classes are never generated. Compile them with Tailwind first, then inline the output.

## All entrypoints

Compiled entrypoints are finished CSS. `/tw` entrypoints publish the uncompiled source from `tw/`, beside `dist/`, which a Tailwind v4 build must process. A focused `/tw` component entrypoint includes the theme tokens, so its classes need nothing else from the package, but it needs `@import "tailwindcss";` before it; see [Tailwind CSS v4 → Using a focused entrypoint](docs/integrating/tailwind.md#using-a-focused-entrypoint).

Each import path resolves the same file under the `style`, `import`, and `default` export conditions. A `types` condition comes first and names an empty declaration, so TypeScript accepts a side-effect import such as `import "@codenhub/styles";` with `noUncheckedSideEffectImports`, which TypeScript 6 turns on by default. A CSS import is a side effect, so make sure your bundler does not drop it as unused.

| Import path                      | What it contains and what it changes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@codenhub/styles`               | Compiled complete stylesheet: Tailwind's base and theme output, tokens, typography, layout and content helpers, components, and the reset. Applies the global reset, root theme, and focus rules.                                                                                                                    |
| `@codenhub/styles/theme`         | Compiled tokens and the intent, presentation, elevation, and corner-pattern classes. Sets root theme properties and the light and dark selectors. No reset and no components.                                                                                                                                        |
| `@codenhub/styles/palette`       | Generated `--palette-*` custom properties: every intent and presentation combination's fill, text, and border color as a flat value, plus flat `border`, `surface`, and `text` colors. For code that cannot use the package itself; see [Customizing → Generated palette](docs/usage/customizing.md#generated-palette). |
| `@codenhub/styles/components`    | Compiled tokens, typography helpers, and every component class. Each component carries its own reduced-motion rule, and the closed-`<dialog>` fix comes with `.card`. No reset, no layout or content helpers, no classless mappings.                                                                                 |
| `@codenhub/styles/native`        | Compiled tokens, typography, layout and content helpers, components, and the package reset, plus [classless mappings](#classless-html) for plain HTML elements. Not Tailwind's Preflight. Applies the reset and broad element selectors.                                                                             |
| `@codenhub/styles/aesthetics`    | All six compiled aesthetics, `.neobrutalism`, `.glass`, `.pixel`, `.chunky-tile`, `.cyber`, and `.sketch`, each with its `-solo` class. No tokens or components of its own; import it in any order.                                                                                                                  |
| `@codenhub/styles/aesthetics/*`  | One compiled aesthetic and its solo class: `/neobrutalism`, `/glass`, `/pixel`, `/chunky-tile`, `/cyber`, or `/sketch`.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `@codenhub/styles/tw`            | Source version of the complete stylesheet. Imports Tailwind itself, then the theme, typography, helpers, components, and reset. Same global rules.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `@codenhub/styles/tw/theme`      | Source theme, tokens, and axis classes. Imports Tailwind's theme layer, emits the theme selectors, and defines the package's `dark:` variant.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `@codenhub/styles/tw/components` | Source theme, typography, buttons, feedback, forms, surfaces, and tooltips. No reset, no layout or content helpers, no classless mappings.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `@codenhub/styles/tw/surface`    | Source theme plus `.surface`, `.card`, and `.panel`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `@codenhub/styles/tw/button`     | Source theme plus `.btn`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `@codenhub/styles/tw/form`       | Source theme plus `.field`, `.text-control`, `.ipt`, `.textarea`, `.select`, `.input-group`, `.checkbox`, `.radio`, and `.switch`.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `@codenhub/styles/tw/feedback`   | Source theme plus `.alert`, `.badge`, `.skeleton`, and `.progress`, with their animations.                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `@codenhub/styles/tw/tooltip`    | Source theme plus the tooltip classes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `@codenhub/styles/tw/reset`      | Source theme, typography helpers, and the global reset. Changes the root, body, and elements, and sets selection, motion, focus, scrollbar, and forced-colors rules.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `@codenhub/styles/tw/native`     | Source version of `/native`: everything but Tailwind's Preflight, plus the package reset and the classless mappings. The broadest global effect.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `@codenhub/styles/tw/typography` | Source theme plus the typography helpers. Sets the theme selectors; no reset, no classless mappings.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `@codenhub/styles/tw/utilities`  | Source theme and typography plus the layout and content helpers.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `@codenhub/styles/tw/aesthetics` | All six aesthetics as source. `/tw/aesthetics/neobrutalism`, `/glass`, `/pixel`, `/chunky-tile`, `/cyber`, and `/sketch` publish one each. Plain CSS with no theme or reset side effects.                                                                                                                            |
| `@codenhub/styles/package.json`  | The package manifest, as JSON. For tools that read the installed version or export map; it is not a stylesheet.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

Do not import two entrypoints that overlap, such as `@codenhub/styles` and `@codenhub/styles/components`, in one build unless duplicated CSS is acceptable. Pick the narrowest entrypoint that covers what a page needs.

## Classless HTML

`@codenhub/styles/native` styles plain HTML elements without any classes, for content you cannot add classes to, such as Markdown output or a CMS body. It holds everything the complete stylesheet does except Tailwind's Preflight, the browser-default reset that `@codenhub/styles` brings with Tailwind. The package's own reset is in it: box sizing, the root background, text color and font, the margin reset on headings, paragraphs, and lists, selection colors, focus rings, and the reduced-motion rule. Then it adds these mappings:

| Element                                                                                                                                        | Styled as                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `h1`, `h2`, `h3`, `h4`, `h5` and `h6`                                                                                                          | `.text-title-lg`, `.text-title`, `.text-title-sm`, `.text-label-lg`, `.text-label` |
| `body`                                                                                                                                         | `.text-body`, inherited by paragraphs, list items, and other text                  |
| `table`                                                                                                                                        | `.data-table`                                                                      |
| `kbd`, `blockquote`, `q`, `code`, `pre`                                                                                                        | `.kbd`, `.quote`, `.quote-inline`, `.code`, `.pre`                                 |
| `hr`                                                                                                                                           | `.divider`                                                                         |
| `input` with no type, or type `text`, `number`, `email`, `password`, `url`, `tel`, `search`, `month`, `week`, `time`, `date`, `datetime-local` | `.ipt`                                                                             |
| `textarea`, `select`                                                                                                                           | `.textarea`, `.select`                                                             |
| `input type="checkbox"`, `input type="radio"`                                                                                                  | `.checkbox`, `.radio`                                                              |
| `button`, `input type="button"`, `type="submit"`, `type="reset"`                                                                               | `.btn`                                                                             |
| `dialog`                                                                                                                                       | `.card.floating`: hidden until opened, then a centered floating card               |
| `progress`                                                                                                                                     | `.progress`, filled to its `value`; with no `value` it is the indeterminate sweep  |

```html
<article>
  <h2>Two-factor authentication</h2>
  <p>Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> to open the command menu.</p>
  <label for="code">Verification code</label>
  <input id="code" type="text" inputmode="numeric" />
  <label><input type="checkbox" /> Remember this device</label>
  <button type="submit">Verify</button>
</article>
```

What it does not do:

- **Some input types are left alone:** `file`, `range`, `color`, and `hidden` keep the browser's own look.
- **No switch.** A checkbox with `role="switch"` is still painted as a checkbox; the mapping does not read roles. A page that needs switches is better served by the class-based stylesheet.
- **Links keep the text around them.** A link inside a heading stays heading-sized; a link is never styled as a button.
- **Body text is set once.** `p` and `li` take their type from the element they sit in, so a container that sets its own size, weight, or tracking applies it to the Markdown inside it. Controls keep their own tracking: a button, a badge, and a text field print `normal`, whatever the page or the container sets.
- **Native behavior stays native.** A `<dialog>` opens with `show()` or `showModal()` as usual; the mapping only paints it. A `<progress>` sweep stops under a reduced-motion preference, and in forced colors the bar uses the system colors.
- **`pre code` is not double-styled.** Code inside a `pre` drops the chip it would draw on its own: background, padding, border, shadow, glow, and clip.

The mappings are global: every matching element on the page is styled, including elements inside third-party widgets. They sit in the `base` [cascade layer](#cascade-layers), so any class beats them. Add an intent or presentation class to a mapped element, such as `<button class="destructive">`, and it applies as it would on `.btn`.

## Cascade layers

Every entrypoint puts its CSS into Tailwind's four cascade layers and declares their order before using one, so the result does not depend on which file loads first:

| Layer        | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `theme`      | Tailwind's theme, the foundation tokens, the theme selectors, and `/palette`.                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `base`       | The reset and the classless element styles.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `components` | The aesthetic classes and the neutral intent values every component starts from.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `utilities`  | Every component (`.btn`, `.card`, `.ipt`, and so on), next to your own Tailwind utilities. The intent, presentation, edge, elevation, corner, and size classes sit in `utilities.families`, a sublayer that loses to every other rule in `utilities`. |
| _unlayered_  | The forced-colors and reduced-motion overrides, the closed-`<dialog>` fix, and the `-solo` classes.                                                                                                                                                   |

What that means when you write your own CSS:

- **Your utility or unlayered CSS beats an intent, presentation, elevation, or aesthetic class** on the same element. `[--ui-fill:50%]` on a `.solid` button, `font-serif` on a `.pixel` region, or `.my-card { --ui-radius-surface: 0 }` in your own stylesheet all apply.
- **A component and your utility share the `utilities` layer.** Specificity decides between them, then source order, as between any two utilities. Your unlayered CSS always beats a component.
- **Your utility beats a component's inner defaults.** `p-0 text-center` on a table cell, `text-sm` on a `.label`, or `px-8` on a `.btn.sm` applies, because the component writes those defaults so that a class on the element wins.
- **State beats your intent.** A field with `aria-invalid="true"` stays destructive even with an intent utility on it.
- **The `-solo` classes are unlayered on purpose**, so they beat a third-party component's layered or zero-specificity styles. A more specific unlayered rule, or an equally specific one that loads later, still beats them; see [Solo classes](docs/usage/solo.md).

## Next

With the shell on the page, continue to [Building a screen](docs/concepts.md) to add a card, a form heading, and a Save button. If you use one of the frameworks above and have not wired it yet, do that first.

<!-- Source: docs/integrating/index.md -->

# Integrating

This section is a detour from the main reading path, for projects whose framework decides where global CSS may go. The package has no JavaScript and no framework bindings (see [Introduction](docs/index.md#what-it-does-not-do)), so integrating it is only about two things: where your framework lets you load a global stylesheet, and whether the project runs Tailwind CSS v4. Follow the one guide that matches your stack, then return to [Building a screen](docs/concepts.md).

## The shared model

Every stack does the same two imports, from the same kind of place — a root layout, an app entry file, or a global CSS file, never a page or a component further down the tree:

1. One [entrypoint](docs/setup.md#all-entrypoints) — the compiled `@codenhub/styles` for any build, or `@codenhub/styles/tw` when the project already runs Tailwind CSS v4.
2. `@codenhub/styles/aesthetics` (or `/tw/aesthetics`) after it, only if the project uses an [aesthetic](docs/usage/aesthetics.md).

Importing from one place matters for two reasons. Some frameworks only _allow_ global CSS from a designated root file and fail the build otherwise — Next.js's Pages Router is one, see [Next.js → Troubleshooting](docs/integrating/nextjs.md#troubleshooting). Where a framework allows it more broadly, as Next.js's App Router does, importing from the root remains the recommended choice for predictable CSS ordering — and importing per-component instead would load the same reset and token rules once per component rather than once per app.

## Which guide to follow

| Stack                                                                         | Guide                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| A Tailwind CSS v4 project on any bundler                                      | [Tailwind CSS v4](docs/integrating/tailwind.md)            |
| Next.js / React                                                               | [Next.js](docs/integrating/nextjs.md)                      |
| Vue                                                                           | [Vue](docs/integrating/vue.md)                             |
| Svelte / SvelteKit                                                            | [Svelte](docs/integrating/svelte.md)                       |
| Astro                                                                         | [Astro](docs/integrating/astro.md)                         |
| Plain HTML, Rails, Laravel, Django, or any app with no Node.js CSS build step | [Without a bundler](docs/integrating/without-a-bundler.md) |

A project with no framework — a plain Vite, webpack, or Parcel build — imports the compiled stylesheet from the project's existing global CSS entry, as [Setup → Import the stylesheet](docs/setup.md#import-the-stylesheet) shows. Vite and webpack resolve the package name as it is; Parcel and PostCSS with `postcss-import` need the change below. The compiled stylesheet holds every class; to ship only the ones your pages use without adopting Tailwind, write a trimmed stylesheet with the package's [`build` command](docs/integrating/without-a-bundler.md#build-only-the-classes-you-use) and import that instead.

### Bundlers that need a nudge

Both tools find the stylesheet once they are told how; neither needs a different entrypoint.

**Parcel.** Turn on its support for a package's `exports` map in your `package.json`:

```json
{
  "@parcel/resolver-default": {
    "packageExports": true
  }
}
```

Then import the package with Parcel's `npm:` prefix, which tells it the name is a package and not a file next to the stylesheet:

```css
@import "npm:@codenhub/styles";
```

**PostCSS with `postcss-import`.** The plugin does not read a package's `exports` map, so the package name alone does not resolve. Import the compiled file by its path on disk instead, relative to your own stylesheet, the same file a `<link>` would name:

```css
@import "../node_modules/@codenhub/styles/dist/index.css";
```

The other compiled entrypoints work the same way, such as `@codenhub/styles/dist/aesthetics/neobrutalism.css`.

## Verifying it worked

After the import, render one styled element and confirm it picked up the package's tokens rather than the browser default:

```html
<button class="btn primary">Save changes</button>
```

A rounded button filled with the primary color (near-black on a light page, near-white on a dark one) means the stylesheet loaded. Unstyled browser-default text most often means the import specifier didn't resolve — check the [entrypoint table](docs/setup.md#all-entrypoints) for the exact specifier to import, and confirm your build tooling resolves package CSS imports at all, see [Setup → Requirements](docs/setup.md#requirements). With no build tool, link the file by its path instead; see [Without a bundler](docs/integrating/without-a-bundler.md). [Setup → When nothing is styled](docs/setup.md#when-nothing-is-styled) lists the other common causes.

## Next

Once the button renders, go back to the main path: [Building a screen](docs/concepts.md) adds the first card and form to the settings page.

<!-- Source: docs/integrating/tailwind.md -->

# Tailwind CSS v4

A project that already runs Tailwind CSS v4 can compile this package's source instead of loading its compiled output. Your app's utilities and the package's classes then come out of one build, share one theme, and use one `dark:` variant. This page covers the import, aesthetics, the focused entrypoints, building your own components with `@apply`, dropping Tailwind's palette, and the build problems you are likely to meet.

## Why source instead of compiled

`/tw` entrypoints publish copied, uncompiled source from the package's `tw/` folder; your own Tailwind build compiles it alongside your app, so its `@theme`, `@utility`, and `@apply` directives resolve together with yours. The compiled entrypoints (`@codenhub/styles`) still work in a Tailwind project, but then two separate CSS pipelines run side by side instead of one — use `/tw` unless a specific reason rules it out.

## Import the source entrypoint

```css
@import "@codenhub/styles/tw";

@source "./src";
```

`/tw` imports Tailwind itself, so it replaces your own `@import "tailwindcss"` rather than joining it: with both, Tailwind's Preflight is emitted twice. Every other `/tw/*` entrypoint expects your import to come first; see [Using a focused entrypoint](#using-a-focused-entrypoint).

Tailwind CSS v4 scans your project automatically — most projects need nothing beyond the import above. `@source` paths resolve relative to the CSS file that declares them, not your project root, so `./src` here means "the `src/` next to this stylesheet"; adjust it to match where your own global stylesheet actually lives. Add `@source` only for markup Tailwind's automatic scan won't reach on its own: a path excluded by default (`.gitignore`d, or inside `node_modules` — an external component library, for instance) or, in a monorepo, one outside this file's own directory tree. Point it at your app's markup, not at this package: the package's source names every class it defines, so scanning it emits all of them whether your pages use them or not.

## Add aesthetics

Add an aesthetic from the source entrypoint the same way as the compiled one, after the base import:

```css
@import "@codenhub/styles/tw";
@import "@codenhub/styles/tw/aesthetics";

@source "./src";
```

## Using a focused entrypoint

Import a focused `/tw/*` entrypoint instead of the combined one — such as `/tw/button` or `/tw/form` — when a build only needs one component family; see the full [entrypoint table](docs/setup.md#all-entrypoints) for what each one composes.

Unlike `/tw`, the focused entrypoints and `/tw/native` do not import Tailwind, so keep your own import first:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@codenhub/styles/tw/button";
```

## Build your own components with `@apply`

On `/tw`, every component, helper, and axis class is a Tailwind utility. That includes the intents (`neutral`, `primary`, `secondary`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`, `info`), the presentation (`solid`, `soft`, `ghost`, `edged`, `edgeless`), the elevation (`flat`, `raised`, `floating`), the corner patterns (`cut-diagonal`, `cut-diagonal-reverse`), and the sizes (`sm`, `lg`). So one class of yours can carry a whole recipe:

```css
@import "@codenhub/styles/tw";

@utility btn-save {
  @apply btn primary soft sm;
}

@utility btn-danger {
  @apply btn destructive md:lg dark:solid;
}
```

```html
<button class="btn-save" type="submit">Save</button>
```

- **An applied component behaves like the class.** `btn-save` hovers, presses, takes focus, and follows an aesthetic the way `class="btn primary soft sm"` does.
- **Variants work.** `hover:primary`, `md:lg`, and `dark:solid` apply an axis class under that condition, in your markup or inside `@apply`.
- **Write your class as `@utility`.** It then stays in the `utilities` layer, so your other utilities on the same element still beat it. A plain `.btn-save { @apply … }` rule works too, but it is unlayered, so what it applies beats every utility on the element; [Customizing → Composition helpers](docs/usage/customizing.md#composition-helpers) has the details.
- **Modifiers apply too.** A component's modifiers, such as `.tight` on `.stack`, `.icon` on `.btn`, or `.interactive` on `.card`, are utilities as well, so `@apply stack tight`, `@apply btn icon pill`, and `md:tight` work. The disabled state is the exception: it stays an attribute or the `.disabled` class in markup.
- **Your utility beats a component's inner defaults.** `p-0 text-center` on a `.data-table` cell, `text-sm` on a `.label`, and `px-8` on a `.btn.sm` all apply.

[Presets](docs/usage/presets.md) compares this with the other ways to set a look once.

## Drop Tailwind's palette

`/tw` builds on Tailwind's default theme, so Tailwind's palette utilities, such as `bg-red-500`, stay available. If your design uses only the package's tokens, clear the hues you do not use:

```css
@import "@codenhub/styles/tw";

@theme {
  --color-red-*: initial;
  --color-orange-*: initial;
  --color-yellow-*: initial;
  --color-lime-*: initial;
  --color-green-*: initial;
  --color-teal-*: initial;
  --color-cyan-*: initial;
  --color-sky-*: initial;
  --color-blue-*: initial;
  --color-violet-*: initial;
  --color-purple-*: initial;
  --color-fuchsia-*: initial;
  --color-pink-*: initial;
  --color-slate-*: initial;
  --color-gray-*: initial;
  --color-zinc-*: initial;
  --color-stone-*: initial;
  --color-black: initial;
}
```

The package's own colors do not change, and you can still add colors of your own in the same block.

The block leaves out `neutral`, `emerald`, `amber`, `rose`, `indigo`, and `white` on purpose: the theme builds its colors from them.

- **Do not clear the whole namespace.** `--color-*: initial` also removes the package's semantic colors, and the build stops with an error such as `Cannot apply unknown utility class`.
- **Do not clear a ramp the theme reads.** Clearing `--color-emerald-*` builds without an error, but the success colors made from it are lost.
- **Do not clear the type, font, or spacing namespaces.** The components apply Tailwind's `text-*` and `font-*` utilities and its `--spacing()` function, so `--text-*: initial`, `--font-*: initial`, `--spacing: initial`, or `--*: initial` stops the build with `Cannot apply unknown utility class` or `The --spacing(…) function requires that the --spacing theme variable exists`. Override single values instead, such as `--text-sm`. Clearing `--radius-*` is safe.

## Troubleshooting

**Classes resolve to no styling**

- **What happened:** components use documented classes like `.btn.primary`, but no styling appears even though `@import "@codenhub/styles/tw"` is in the stylesheet.
- **Why:** this is rarely `@source` itself — Tailwind already scans your project automatically. The more common cause is markup living somewhere that automatic scan excludes by default: a `.gitignore`d path, or a component pulled from `node_modules`. Tailwind may not see a class used only there and skips generating a rule for it.
- **Fix:** add an explicit `@source` pointing at that directory, resolved relative to this stylesheet — matching the [example above](#import-the-source-entrypoint).

**Duplicate token and reset rules**

- **What happened:** the built stylesheet is larger than expected, and browser devtools show the same custom properties or reset rules defined twice.
- **Why:** one of two things. Importing both a compiled entrypoint (`@codenhub/styles`) and a `/tw` entrypoint (`@codenhub/styles/tw`) in the same build compiles the same tokens and reset from two independent sources; Tailwind's build has no way to know they describe the same package. Or your stylesheet imports `tailwindcss` beside `/tw`, which already imports it, so Preflight is emitted twice.
- **Fix:** pick one path per project — `/tw` entrypoints for a project running Tailwind CSS v4, compiled entrypoints everywhere else — and drop your own `@import "tailwindcss"` when you import `/tw`.

**A class built at runtime has no styling**

- **What happened:** `<button class="btn primary">` is styled, but a button whose class comes from a variable, such as `"btn " + variant`, or from CMS content, is not.
- **Why:** Tailwind emits only the classes it finds written out in the files it scans. That holds for the package's component classes too: a `/tw` build emits `.alert` only if `alert` appears somewhere it scans, which keeps the stylesheet to what your pages use. The intent, presentation, elevation, corner, and size classes, such as `.primary`, `.soft`, and `.sm`, are utilities too, so the same holds for them. The aesthetic classes, such as `.glass`, are plain CSS and always emitted. A name assembled at runtime never appears whole in a file, so the scan misses it.
- **Fix:** write each complete class name somewhere Tailwind scans, for example in a lookup object (`{ save: "btn primary", remove: "btn destructive" }`), or list the names your code or content can produce in your stylesheet:

```css
@import "@codenhub/styles/tw";

@source inline("btn alert badge primary destructive soft");
```

Every `/tw` entrypoint requires Tailwind CSS 4.3.2 or newer, below 5 (`>=4.3.2 <5`).

## The `dark:` variant

The `/tw` entrypoints define their own `dark:` variant, so your utilities switch with the same light and dark selectors the package's tokens use. It has one known difference from the tokens when themes are nested; see [Theming → The dark: variant](docs/usage/theming.md#the-dark-variant).

## Next

Return to the main path: [Building a screen](docs/concepts.md) adds the first card and form to the settings page. Everything it shows works the same on `/tw`.

<!-- Source: docs/integrating/nextjs.md -->

# Next.js

Next.js has two router architectures, and they treat global CSS differently:

- **App Router** (an `app/` directory): global CSS — including an external package's stylesheet like this one — can be imported from any layout, page, or component under `app/`. Importing it from the root layout is only a recommendation, for predictable CSS ordering across routes; Next.js does not enforce it and no error occurs if you import it elsewhere.
- **Pages Router** (a `pages/` directory, no `app/`): global CSS is restricted to `pages/_app.tsx`. Importing it from anywhere else fails the build — Next.js enforces this itself, not this package; see [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting).
- **Both directories present** (mid-migration): import the stylesheet in both root files. The two routers serve their own routes independently, so a route under `pages/` never sees a stylesheet imported only in `app/layout.tsx`, and vice versa.

## Import the stylesheet

Add the import to the root file for your router:

**App Router**

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
import "@codenhub/styles";

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>{children}</body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

**Pages Router**

```tsx
// pages/_app.tsx
import "@codenhub/styles";
import type { AppProps } from "next/app";

export default function App({ Component, pageProps }: AppProps) {
  return <Component {...pageProps} />;
}
```

Running Tailwind CSS v4? `@import "@codenhub/styles/tw"` is a CSS directive, so it belongs in a CSS file, not a bare import in `layout.tsx`/`_app.tsx` — add it (with `@source` if needed; `/tw` imports Tailwind itself, so leave out your own `@import "tailwindcss"`) to your global CSS file, and import that file from the same root file shown above instead. See [Tailwind CSS v4](docs/integrating/tailwind.md).

## Force a theme

Apply `.dark` or `.light` on `<html>` to force a theme instead of following the system preference; see [Theming → Light and dark](docs/usage/theming.md#light-and-dark).

```tsx
<html lang="en" className="dark">
```

## Troubleshooting

**Pages Router build fails with "Global CSS cannot be imported from files other than your Custom `<App>`"**

- **What happened:** Next.js rejected a global CSS `import` statement outside `pages/_app.tsx`. This restriction is specific to the Pages Router — Next.js enforces it itself, not this package, and it applies to any global CSS import, not specifically to `@codenhub/styles`. It does not apply to the App Router, where the same import works from any layout, page, or component.
- **Why:** the Pages Router has no per-route CSS boundary the way the App Router does, so Next.js requires one predictable file for global stylesheets to avoid ordering conflicts between pages.
- **Fix:** move the `import "@codenhub/styles"` line to `pages/_app.tsx`, and remove it from wherever it currently is.

## Next

Return to the main path: [Building a screen](docs/concepts.md) adds the first card and form to the settings page. [Setup → All entrypoints](docs/setup.md#all-entrypoints) lists every other stylesheet you can import.

<!-- Source: docs/integrating/vue.md -->

# Vue

Vue places no restriction on where CSS is imported from, but importing it once, from the app's entry file, keeps the reset and tokens from loading more than once and guarantees they're in place before any component renders.

## Import the stylesheet

```ts
// main.ts
import "@codenhub/styles";
import { createApp } from "vue";
import App from "./App.vue";

createApp(App).mount("#app");
```

Running Tailwind CSS v4? Import `@codenhub/styles/tw` from a CSS entry file instead of `main.ts`, using the `@tailwindcss/vite` plugin — see [Tailwind CSS v4](docs/integrating/tailwind.md).

## Force a theme

Apply `.dark` or `.light` on the root element to force a theme instead of following the system preference; see [Theming → Light and dark](docs/usage/theming.md#light-and-dark).

## Next

Return to the main path: [Building a screen](docs/concepts.md) adds the first card and form to the settings page. [Setup → All entrypoints](docs/setup.md#all-entrypoints) lists every other stylesheet you can import.

<!-- Source: docs/integrating/svelte.md -->

# Svelte

Svelte and SvelteKit let you import CSS from any component, but the package's reset and tokens should load once, before any component renders. This page shows where that one import goes in SvelteKit and in a plain Svelte app.

## Import the stylesheet

**SvelteKit** — import from the root layout so it loads once for every route:

```svelte
<!-- src/routes/+layout.svelte -->
<script>
  import "@codenhub/styles";
  let { children } = $props();
</script>

{@render children()}
```

**Plain Svelte + Vite** — import from the entry file instead:

```ts
// main.ts
import "@codenhub/styles";
import { mount } from "svelte";
import App from "./App.svelte";

mount(App, { target: document.getElementById("app")! });
```

Running Tailwind CSS v4? Import `@codenhub/styles/tw` from the app's CSS entry instead — see [Tailwind CSS v4](docs/integrating/tailwind.md).

## Force a theme

Apply `.dark` or `.light` on `<html>` (edit `src/app.html` in SvelteKit) to force a theme instead of following the system preference; see [Theming → Light and dark](docs/usage/theming.md#light-and-dark).

## Next

Return to the main path: [Building a screen](docs/concepts.md) adds the first card and form to the settings page. [Setup → All entrypoints](docs/setup.md#all-entrypoints) lists every other stylesheet you can import.

<!-- Source: docs/integrating/astro.md -->

# Astro

Astro renders components statically by default, but a global stylesheet import still only needs to happen once — from a shared layout, not from individual pages or islands.

## Import the stylesheet

```astro
---
// src/layouts/Layout.astro
import "@codenhub/styles";
---

<html lang="en">
  <body>
    <slot />
  </body>
</html>
```

Every page that uses this layout loads the stylesheet once. Running Tailwind CSS v4? Import `@codenhub/styles/tw` through Astro's Tailwind integration instead — see [Tailwind CSS v4](docs/integrating/tailwind.md), including when an explicit `@source` is actually needed.

## Force a theme

Apply `.dark` or `.light` on `<html>` to force a theme instead of following the system preference; see [Theming → Light and dark](docs/usage/theming.md#light-and-dark).

## Next

Return to the main path: [Building a screen](docs/concepts.md) adds the first card and form to the settings page. [Setup → All entrypoints](docs/setup.md#all-entrypoints) lists every other stylesheet you can import.

<!-- Source: docs/integrating/without-a-bundler.md -->

# Without a bundler

The compiled stylesheets are finished CSS: each one is a single file with no `@import` and no reference to another file, and every image it draws is embedded as a `data:` URL: the checkbox tick and dash masks, and the SVG lens filters `.glass-liquid` uses. A page can load one with a plain `<link>` tag, from any server, with no build step, and the stylesheet makes no further requests.

What needs a build tool is the import _name_. `@import "@codenhub/styles"` names a package, and finding the file behind that name — `node_modules/@codenhub/styles/dist/index.css` — is done by Node-aware tooling such as Vite, webpack, or the Tailwind CLI, which read the package's `exports` map. A browser does not: it resolves an `@import` URL against the stylesheet that contains it and a `<link href>` against the page, so a bare package name becomes a request for a path that does not exist. Without a bundler, link the file by its path instead.

The `/tw` entrypoints are Tailwind source and need a Tailwind build. `/tw/aesthetics` is the exception, plain CSS with nothing for Tailwind to process, but without a bundler link the compiled `dist/aesthetics/` files instead, as below. This page is for a page that has no Node.js CSS build: plain HTML, Rails, Laravel, Django, or any server-rendered app. There are two paths:

1. **Link the compiled stylesheet.** It needs nothing but static files. You ship every class, whether your pages use it or not.
2. **Build a stylesheet with the package's `chs build` command.** It scans your templates and writes a stylesheet with only the classes they use. See [Build only the classes you use](#build-only-the-classes-you-use).

## Which file to link

Each compiled import path is one file in the package's `dist/` folder:

| Import path                     | File                                                              |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@codenhub/styles`              | `dist/index.css`                                                  |
| `@codenhub/styles/theme`        | `dist/theme.css`                                                  |
| `@codenhub/styles/components`   | `dist/components.css`                                             |
| `@codenhub/styles/native`       | `dist/native.css`                                                 |
| `@codenhub/styles/palette`      | `dist/palette.css`                                                |
| `@codenhub/styles/aesthetics`   | `dist/aesthetics/index.css`                                       |
| `@codenhub/styles/aesthetics/*` | `dist/aesthetics/<name>.css`, such as `dist/aesthetics/pixel.css` |

Link one base file, not several, since they overlap, and any aesthetics you use. Their order does not matter, because every file declares the [cascade layers](docs/setup.md#cascade-layers) before using one. [Setup → All entrypoints](docs/setup.md#all-entrypoints) explains what each one contains.

## From a CDN

jsDelivr and unpkg serve every file of every published npm version, so a page can link one with nothing installed:

```html
<head>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@codenhub/styles@0.8.0/dist/index.css" />
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@codenhub/styles@0.8.0/dist/aesthetics/pixel.css" />
</head>
```

Put the exact version in the URL. Without one, the CDN serves the latest release, and below 1.0 a minor release may rename or remove a class; see [Versioning](docs/index.md#versioning).

## From your own server

Install the package, then serve its `dist/` folder as static files:

```sh
npm install @codenhub/styles
```

How a framework serves a folder from `node_modules` differs, so each one is below. Where the framework reads the folder in place, as Rails and Django do, upgrading the package and redeploying is all an update takes.

### Plain HTML

Copy `node_modules/@codenhub/styles/dist` into the folder your server publishes, then link it:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/vendor/codenhub-styles/index.css" />
```

Repeat the copy after each upgrade, for example from an npm `postinstall` script.

### Ruby on Rails

A Rails app built with `cssbundling-rails` already runs a bundler: import the package from `app/assets/stylesheets/application.css` as in [Setup → Import the stylesheet](docs/setup.md#import-the-stylesheet).

With Propshaft and no CSS bundler, add the package's folder to the asset paths:

```ruby
# config/initializers/assets.rb
Rails.application.config.assets.paths << Rails.root.join("node_modules/@codenhub")
```

Then link it from the layout, by its path below that folder:

```erb
<%# app/views/layouts/application.html.erb %>
<%= stylesheet_link_tag "styles/dist/index" %>
<%= stylesheet_link_tag "styles/dist/aesthetics/pixel" %>
```

Point the path at `node_modules/@codenhub` rather than at `dist/` itself. Propshaft serves files by their path below each asset folder, so adding `dist/` directly would publish a bare `index.css` that collides with any `index.css` of your own.

The files you link are in `dist/`, which holds only finished CSS, plus an empty `index.d.ts` for TypeScript. The Tailwind source lives in `tw/`, outside `dist/`, so a static pipeline that serves or fingerprints `dist/` meets no `@import` it cannot resolve.

### Django

Add the folder to `STATICFILES_DIRS` under a prefix, which keeps its file names apart from your own static files:

```python
# settings.py
STATICFILES_DIRS = [
    ("codenhub-styles", BASE_DIR / "node_modules/@codenhub/styles/dist"),
]
```

```django
{% load static %}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'codenhub-styles/index.css' %}" />
```

Point the prefix at `dist`, not at the package folder. `dist/` holds only finished CSS, plus an empty `index.d.ts` for TypeScript that the storage copies as it is, so `collectstatic` also works with `ManifestStaticFilesStorage`, which fingerprints each file and rewrites the references inside it. The package folder also holds the Tailwind source in `tw/`, whose `@import "tailwindcss/..."` lines that storage cannot resolve.

### Laravel

A Laravel app runs Vite by default, so it has a bundler: import the package from `resources/css/app.css` as in [Setup → Import the stylesheet](docs/setup.md#import-the-stylesheet), and load that file with the `@vite` directive as usual.

## Build only the classes you use

The package carries a command, `chs`, that reads your templates for class names and writes one minified stylesheet with only the StyleKit classes they use. A page that uses one button gets about an eighth of the full stylesheet; the exact size depends on which classes you use, since each component brings the shared rules it relies on.

The command works with a bundler too. A project whose bundler does not run Tailwind, such as a plain Vite or webpack build, can write the stylesheet into its sources, `--output src/stylekit.css`, and import that file where it would import `@codenhub/styles`. A project that runs Tailwind CSS v4 gets the same trimming from the [source entrypoint](docs/integrating/tailwind.md) and does not need the command.

It needs Node.js 24 or newer on the machine that builds the CSS, whether that is your laptop, a CI job, or a deploy step, and nothing else: the package is the whole install, with no Tailwind and no configuration. Install it as a development dependency from your project root; npm creates a `package.json` if you have none:

```sh
npm install --save-dev @codenhub/styles
```

The stylesheet the command writes is plain CSS, so the servers that serve your site need neither Node.js nor the package. Add the build to your `package.json` scripts, where the installed command is on the path by its name:

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "build:css": "chs build --content \"app/views/**/*.erb\" --output public/stylekit.css"
  }
}
```

Then run it from your project root:

```sh
npm run build:css
```

To run it once without a script, call it through the package name:

```sh
npx @codenhub/styles build --content "app/views/**/*.erb" --output public/stylekit.css
```

Do not type `npx chs`. `chs` is the command's name inside this package, but npm also has an unrelated package called `chs`, and `npx chs` runs that one in any folder where this package is not installed.

On success the command prints one line, the absolute path it wrote and the file's size in bytes:

```text
/home/you/shop/public/stylekit.css 24497 bytes
```

Link that file from your layout like any static stylesheet.

### Rails views

```json
"build:css": "chs build --content \"app/views/**/*.erb\" --content \"app/helpers/**/*.rb\" --output public/stylekit.css"
```

```erb
<%# app/views/layouts/application.html.erb %>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/stylekit.css" />
```

### Laravel Blade views

```json
"build:css": "chs build --content \"resources/views/**/*.blade.php\" --output public/css/stylekit.css"
```

```blade
{{-- resources/views/layouts/app.blade.php --}}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ asset('css/stylekit.css') }}" />
```

### Django templates

A Django project keeps templates in a project-level `templates/` folder, in each app's own `templates/` folder, or both. Give one `--content` for each place yours live, and leave out any place you do not use, since a glob that matches nothing fails the build:

```json
"build:css": "chs build --content \"templates/**/*.html\" --content \"shop/templates/**/*.html\" --output static/stylekit.css"
```

```django
{% load static %}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'stylekit.css' %}" />
```

Write the output into a folder listed in `STATICFILES_DIRS`, here `static/`, so `collectstatic` picks it up. The settings above list only the package's folder, so add `BASE_DIR / "static"` to that list if your project does not have it yet.

### Options

- `--content <glob>`, or `-c <glob>`, names the files to read for class names. It is required and repeatable: pass it once per glob, and the build reads every file any of them matches. A relative glob is resolved against the folder you run the command in, so run it from your project root; an absolute glob is used as given. `**` matches any number of folders, and `{rb,erb}` either extension. Any text file works, whatever its extension. Each glob has to match at least one file, or the build fails and names it, so a typo cannot ship an empty stylesheet. Files your `.gitignore` excludes are still read when a glob matches them, and nothing outside your globs is read.
- Quote every glob, with `\"` inside a `package.json` script. Without quotes, your shell may expand the glob into a list of files before the command sees it, and only the first file counts as the `--content` value. When that leaves extra file names behind, the build rejects them rather than silently reading less than you meant; when the glob matched a single file, the build reads just that file and nothing your templates add later.
- `--output <file>`, or `-o <file>`, is the stylesheet to write. It is required. A relative path is resolved against the folder you run the command in, missing parent folders are created, and an existing file is replaced.
- `--aesthetic <name>` adds one of the [aesthetics](docs/usage/aesthetics.md): `neobrutalism`, `glass`, `pixel`, `chunky-tile`, `cyber`, or `sketch`. Repeat it for more than one; naming one twice includes it once. Aesthetics are opt-in because the build cannot tell from your templates which one you want: each is added when you ask for it, less its rules for classes your templates do not use, and none is included when you do not.
- `--no-minify` writes readable, indented CSS instead. Useful for reading what the build produced; serve the minified file.
- `--help` prints the usage, with the aesthetics this version ships. `--version` prints the package version. Both build nothing and exit with status 0.

The output always holds the theme, its design tokens as CSS custom properties, the reset, the base rules every component relies on, and the classes a page gets at run time rather than from a template, such as `.theme-dark`. On top of that comes each StyleKit class your templates use. The output is built from the complete stylesheet, not from `/native`, so it has no classless mappings. A build whose templates name every class writes the complete stylesheet, byte for byte.

### How classes are found

The build does not run your templates. It reads each file your `--content` globs match as plain text, collects every word that could be a class name, and writes the rules for the words that are StyleKit classes. This is how Tailwind CSS reads content too.

A class has to appear in a file as one whole word. `class="btn primary"`, `class: "btn primary"`, and `classes = ["btn", "primary"]` all work, and so does a class written before a colon or after one, as in Svelte's `class:primary={isPrimary}` or a Ruby hash's `btn: true`. A word that only looks like a class also counts: a comment that says "card" adds the card's full rules to the stylesheet, which makes the file larger and changes nothing on the page.

A class name your code assembles while rendering never appears whole in any file, so the build cannot find it. In `class="btn <%= @order.priority %>"`, `btn` is found, but the intent is whatever `priority` holds at render time; if that is `destructive`, the button renders without its red. Two ways out:

- **Write class names whole.** Map each value to a complete class name in a file the build reads, such as `{ "urgent" => "destructive", "normal" => "neutral" }.fetch(@order.priority)` in a helper.
- **List them in a safelist file.** A plain text file with one class name per line, added with its own `--content`, such as `--content config/stylekit-classes.txt`. Keep it next to the code that builds the class names, so whoever changes one sees the other.

### Variants

An intent, presentation, or modifier class can take one of ten prefixes, written as in Tailwind: `sm:`, `md:`, `lg:`, `xl:`, and `2xl:` apply it from that breakpoint up, `hover:`, `focus:`, `focus-visible:`, and `active:` while the element is in that state, and `dark:` wherever the dark theme applies, as [Theming → The dark: variant](docs/usage/theming.md#the-dark-variant) describes. `md:lg` makes a button large from the `md` breakpoint, and `hover:primary` gives it the primary intent on hover:

```html
<button class="btn sm md:lg ghost hover:soft">Save</button>
```

That covers intents such as `primary` and `destructive`, the fill and edge classes such as `soft` and `ruled`, and modifiers such as `sm`, `lg`, `raised`, `pill`, and `tight`. `disabled` takes none: it is a state the element is in, so write it as the attribute or the class. Component classes such as `btn` and `card`, and the text and layout helpers, take no prefix.

Each prefix is a fixed copy of those classes, built into the package, so the list is the common ones rather than all of Tailwind's. The command does not stack prefixes, as in `md:hover:primary`, and offers no other ones, such as `print:` or `group-hover:`. Such a class is not found, and the element renders without it.

### What it does not do

- **No Tailwind utilities.** `flex`, `mt-4`, `text-red-500`, and the rest of Tailwind are not StyleKit classes, so the build leaves them out. For layout, StyleKit's own [layout helpers](docs/usage/content-and-layout.md) are in the build like any other class. A project that wants Tailwind's utilities, its other variants, or prefixes stacked runs Tailwind itself and imports the [source entrypoint](docs/integrating/tailwind.md), which gives all three.
- **No watch mode.** It builds once and exits. Run it again after you change a template, from a script, or from a file watcher your framework or editor already has. A class the stylesheet does not have yet leaves its element unstyled until the next build.
- **No configuration file and no custom CSS.** You cannot add your own `@theme` values, `@utility` definitions, or plugins. To change the look, override the custom properties in a stylesheet of your own loaded after this one, as [Customizing](docs/usage/customizing.md) describes.
- **No other commands.** `build` is the only one; `--help` and `--version` are the only flags that run without it.

### In a deploy

Build the stylesheet before whatever step collects or fingerprints your assets, such as `rails assets:precompile`, `php artisan optimize`, or `python manage.py collectstatic`. Either commit the output, so the servers need no Node.js at all at the cost of a generated file someone has to remember to rebuild, or build it on deploy, so the build machine needs Node.js 24 or newer.

Pin the version. Below 1.0 a minor release may rename or remove a class, so the same command can write a different stylesheet with a newer version. The output depends on nothing but the package's version and your templates, so commit `package.json` and the lockfile npm writes, and install with `npm ci` on the build machine, so every build uses the version you tested.

### When the build fails

Every failure prints one line starting with `chs:` to standard error and exits with status 1, without writing the output file, so a deploy script stops instead of shipping a stale or empty stylesheet. The line says what went wrong and what to do:

- **`missing --content` or `missing --output`.** Add the one it names. An `--output` that is empty or only spaces counts as missing.
- **`--content "<glob>" matches no file in <folder>`.** Usually a typo in the path, a command run from another folder than your project root, or a glob for a place your project does not use. Building from nothing would write a stylesheet with no component classes, and the site would quietly lose its styling.
- **`unexpected argument "<file>"`.** Almost always a `--content` glob without quotes, which your shell expanded into a list of files. Quote the glob.
- **`unknown option "<flag>"`.** A typo, or an option from another tool, such as `--watch` or `--config`. `--help` lists the options.
- **`option "<flag>" is missing its value or does not take one`.** A flag that takes a value was the last thing on the line, or `--no-minify` was given one, as in `--no-minify=true`.
- **`unknown aesthetic "<name>"; choose from ...`.** Pick one of the names listed. They are lowercase and hyphenated, as in `chunky-tile`.
- **`missing command` or `unknown command "<name>"`.** The first word after `chs` has to be `build`.
- **`this command needs Node.js 24 or newer`.** Update Node.js on the machine that builds the CSS.
- **`cannot write the stylesheet: <reason>`.** `<reason>` is Node.js's own message. `EISDIR` means `--output` names an existing folder, so name a file inside it; `EACCES` or `EPERM` means you cannot write there.

## Verifying it worked

Render one styled element, as in [Integrating → Verifying it worked](docs/integrating/index.md#verifying-it-worked):

```html
<button class="btn primary">Save changes</button>
```

A rounded button filled with the primary color means the stylesheet loaded. If the button looks like the browser default, open the browser's network panel: a `404` on the stylesheet means the path or the static-file setup is wrong.

## Next

Return to the main path: [Building a screen](docs/concepts.md) adds the first card and form to the settings page. [Setup → All entrypoints](docs/setup.md#all-entrypoints) lists every other stylesheet you can import.

<!-- Source: docs/concepts.md -->

# Building a screen

This page turns the empty shell from [Setup](docs/setup.md) into the first real part of the settings screen: a page header, a profile card with Save and Cancel buttons, and a plan summary beside a usage card. On the way it introduces the three choices every component makes, intent, presentation, and aesthetic, at the moment the screen needs each one. Everything else in these docs builds on this model.

## The smallest screen

A page header and one card with one button:

```html
<main class="section">
  <div class="section-content narrow stack">
    <h1 class="text-title">Account settings</h1>
    <section class="card stack">
```
