| `--intent-border`   | Line color. With no intent it is the aesthetic's `--ui-ink`, then `--color-border`; text controls and toggles read `--ui-control-ink`, then `--ui-ink`, then `--color-control-border`, and tables read `--ui-rule-ink` first. |
| `--intent-fill-max` | How far a fill of this intent may go. `100%` for every intent except neutral.                                                                                                                                                 |

`--intent-color` and `--intent-strong` are not interchangeable. The base color is chosen to be filled with; the strong tone is chosen to be read against the page. A soft or ghost component prints the strong tone, which is why a soft warning reads in amber-800 while a solid one is filled with amber-600.

The strong tone also has to stay recognizably its own hue. On a dark page, the `-100` shade of every family is a pale tint with almost no color at small sizes: a soft success badge and a soft destructive one would both read as white. The dark strong tones are `-300` for that reason, and the tints under them are `-900`, which measures 5.0:1 or better wherever a partial fill holds text, and over 9:1 on the page.

`--intent-border` exists so a neutral border stays the quiet border gray rather than the text color. Everything that draws a line reads it: control borders, table rules, dividers, key caps, and quote bars.

`--intent-fill-max` exists for the neutral intent, whose color is the page's own text color. Every other intent is a hue, readable as a pale tint at 12% and saturated at 100%; a gray filled to 100% is a black or white block, the loudest thing on the page for the intent that means nothing in particular. Neutral stops at `20%`, so `.solid` gives it a quiet gray that is still a step past `.soft`. Hover adds its step on top of the cap, so a capped fill still deepens under the pointer.

The text color follows the fill. `--intent-contrast` is the text color for a full fill; printed on a fifth of one, it would be white on light gray. So contrast text appears only once the fill is past halfway, and reaches full strength at a full fill; below that, a component prints `--intent-strong`. A capped neutral therefore prints the strong tone. A state that lifts the cap on purpose, such as a checked checkbox, reaches a full fill and prints the contrast color.

## Foundation tokens

Foundation tokens set layout, shape, motion, focus, depth, and stacking. Override them on `:root`, or on an element for what is inside it.

The four `--elevation-*` shadows are for elements you style yourself. They are separate from the `.flat`, `.raised`, and `.floating` classes, which scale a component's own shadow and draw nothing until an aesthetic or one of those classes asks for depth; see [Composing → Elevation](docs/usage/composing.md#elevation). Both use the weights none, small, medium, and large, but one is a fixed value and the other scales shadow parts, so they do not always look the same.

| Token                      | Default                                                | Purpose                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--font-default`           | `"Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`                    | Page font. See [Fonts](#fonts).                                                                                 |
| `--container-narrow`       | `48rem`                                                | Width of `.section-content.narrow`.                                                                             |
| `--container-max`          | `80rem`                                                | Width of `.section-content`.                                                                                    |
| `--container-wide`         | `90rem`                                                | Width of `.section-content.wide`.                                                                               |
| `--layout-gutter`          | `clamp(1rem, 4vw, 2rem)`                               | Side padding of `.section`, growing with the window.                                                            |
| `--layout-section-block`   | `clamp(4rem, 9vw, 7rem)`                               | Top and bottom padding of `.section`, growing with the window.                                                  |
| `--layout-gap`             | `1rem`                                                 | Gap of `.view`, `.stack`, `.cluster`, and `.auto-grid`.                                                         |
| `--layout-grid-min`        | `16rem`                                                | Narrowest column of `.auto-grid`.                                                                               |
| `--radius-small`           | `0.25rem`                                              | Corner of small chips: `.kbd` and `.code`.                                                                      |
| `--radius-control`         | `0.5rem`                                               | Corner of buttons, fields, and tooltip bubbles.                                                                 |
| `--radius-surface`         | `0.875rem`                                             | Corner of cards, panels, and alerts.                                                                            |
| `--control-height`         | `2.5rem`                                               | Minimum height of a default button and a text control.                                                          |
| `--border-width`           | `1px`                                                  | Border width.                                                                                                   |
| `--elevation-color`        | `rgb(15 23 42 / 0.08)` light, `rgb(0 0 0 / 0.55)` dark | The shadow color the four elevations use. Heavier on a dark page, where a light shadow would not show.          |
| `--elevation-none`         | `none`                                                 | No shadow.                                                                                                      |
| `--elevation-sm`           | `0 1px 2px`, `0 1px 3px`                               | A light shadow for your own surfaces, such as a card.                                                           |
| `--elevation-md`           | `0 4px 6px -1px`, `0 2px 4px -2px`                     | A shadow for your own raised elements, such as a dropdown menu.                                                 |
| `--elevation-lg`           | `0 20px 25px -5px`, `0 8px 10px -6px`                  | A shadow for your own overlays, such as a modal dialog.                                                         |
| `--focus-ring`             | Not set                                                | Color of the keyboard focus ring. When unset, `--color-primary` at 64% opacity, on the focused element.         |
| `--focus-ring-offset`      | Not set                                                | Distance of the ring from the element. When unset, the ring sits on the element's border under every aesthetic. |
| `--focus-ring-width`       | `3px`                                                  | Width of the keyboard focus ring.                                                                               |
| `--motion-duration-fast`   | `120ms`                                                | A table row's hover.                                                                                            |
| `--motion-duration-normal` | `200ms`                                                | Color, border, shadow, and press transitions, toggle marks, and the tooltip bubble.                             |
| `--motion-duration-slow`   | `400ms`                                                | Progress value changes, and the base of the skeleton and progress shimmer cycle.                                |
| `--motion-ease`            | `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`                           | Easing for every transition.                                                                                    |
| `--z-popover`              | `40`                                                   | Stacking order of tooltip bubbles. Use it for your own popovers so they stack the same way.                     |
| `--breakpoint-xs`          | `30rem`                                                | The `xs:` responsive breakpoint. Only in a `/tw` build; the compiled entrypoints do not declare it.             |

Each `--elevation-*` shadow is made of the listed parts, each in `--elevation-color`. The four shadows are composed once, on the root, so an `--elevation-color` you set on a container does not reach them: set it on `:root`, or set the `--elevation-*` token itself on the container. The elevation classes, such as `.card.raised`, read `--elevation-color` on the element and follow a container's value, with one exception: every aesthetic class sets its own `--elevation-color` on its region. A value set above a `.glass` or `.pixel` region does not reach inside it. Set it on the aesthetic's element itself, where your utility or unlayered CSS beats the class, or on an element inside the region. Under glass, a surface's shadow is built on the `.glass` element, so only a value set there changes it. Under `.neobrutalism` the shadow is drawn in the intent or the ink, and `.cyber` draws no depth, so neither reads the token. The hover step that deepens a fill under the pointer is a presentation token, `--hover-step`; see [Customizing](docs/usage/customizing.md#presentation-tokens).

## Fonts

The package ships no font files and makes no network requests. Every font token names fonts already installed on the reader's device until you supply your own.

| Token            | Read by                                                                                          | Without your value                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--font-default` | The reset, on `html` and `body`, and `.glass` and `.neobrutalism` regions. Controls inherit it.  | `"Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`                                                                                                             |
| `--font-mono`    | The `kbd`, `code`, and `pre` content helpers, and `<kbd>`, `<code>`, and `<pre>` under `/native` | `ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", "Courier New", monospace`. Under `/tw`, your Tailwind theme's value. |
| `--font-pixel`   | [`.pixel`](docs/usage/aesthetics.md#pixel) and `.pixel-solo`                                              | Not declared. Falls back to a monospace stack.                                                                                                  |
| `--font-rounded` | [`.chunky-tile`](docs/usage/aesthetics.md#chunky-tile) and `.chunky-tile-solo`                            | Not declared. Falls back to `--font-default`, then a sans-serif stack.                                                                          |
| `--font-cyber`   | [`.cyber`](docs/usage/aesthetics.md#cyber) and `.cyber-solo`                                              | Not declared. Falls back to a monospace stack.                                                                                                  |
| `--font-sketch`  | [`.sketch`](docs/usage/aesthetics.md#sketch) and `.sketch-solo`                                           | Not declared. Falls back to the platform `cursive` family.                                                                                      |

`--font-default` reaches the page only through the reset, which `@codenhub/styles`, `/native`, `/tw`, `/tw/native`, and `/tw/reset` include. With `/theme` or `/components` alone, set `font-family` on `body` yourself, and set `--font-default` to the same font: `.glass` and `.neobrutalism` regions set their own `font-family` from the token, so a font set only on `body` does not reach inside them. Or set only the token, and write `font-family: var(--font-default)` on `body`. The aesthetic tokens are read by the aesthetic's own class, so they work with any entrypoint.

To use a web font, load it the way you load any font, then name it in the token. Set the token on `:root` for the whole page, or on any element for that part of it:

```html
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" />
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin />
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400..700&display=swap" />
```

```css
:root {
  --font-default: "Inter", system-ui, sans-serif;
}
```

A self-hosted font is declared with `@font-face` and named the same way:

```css
@font-face {
  font-family: "Pixelify Sans";
  src: url("/fonts/pixelify-sans.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight: 400 700;
  font-display: swap;
}

:root {
  --font-pixel: "Pixelify Sans", monospace;
}
```

Load weights 400 to 700, and 800 for `--font-rounded`: components set `font-weight` from 400 to 700, and `.chunky-tile` sets its labels in 800. A browser that lacks a weight fakes it by thickening the regular one, which smears a pixel or handwriting face. Always end the stack with a generic family, such as `sans-serif` or `monospace`, so text still renders while the font loads or if it fails to.

## Next

The screen has your colors in both themes. [Aesthetics](docs/usage/aesthetics.md) changes what it is made of: thick black outlines, frosted glass, pixels, and more.

<!-- Source: docs/usage/aesthetics.md -->

# Aesthetics

The settings screen has your colors. An aesthetic changes what its components are made of: the corners, the thickness of the borders, the shadow, and the shape. Put `.neobrutalism` on the `<main>` of the settings screen and every card, button, field, and badge in it gets square corners, a thick outline in the ink color, and a hard offset shadow, while keeping its colors. This page shows how to add one, then describes each of the six: what it changes, the number you can tune, and where it behaves differently from the default look.

## Add an aesthetic

Aesthetics ship in a separate entrypoint, so load it next to the stylesheet:

```css
@import "@codenhub/styles";
@import "@codenhub/styles/aesthetics";
```

Load order does not matter: the aesthetic classes sit in the `components` cascade layer, and every entrypoint declares the layer order before it uses one, so an aesthetic imported before the base stylesheet wins exactly as one imported after it. See [Setup → Cascade layers](docs/setup.md#cascade-layers).

Then put the class on any element. Unlike intent, an aesthetic passes down: everything inside the element takes it.

```html
<main class="neobrutalism stack">
  <section class="card stack" aria-labelledby="profile-title">…</section>
  <section class="card soft destructive stack" aria-labelledby="danger-title">
    …
    <button class="btn destructive" type="button">Delete account</button>
  </section>
</main>
```

The danger zone keeps its red: under neobrutalism its outline and shadow are red too, because this aesthetic draws them in the component's own intent. To load one aesthetic instead of all six, import it by name, such as `@codenhub/styles/aesthetics/neobrutalism`; [Setup → All entrypoints](docs/setup.md#all-entrypoints) lists them.

| Class           | Look                                                                                                                            |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.neobrutalism` | No radius, a thick ink outline, a hard unblurred offset shadow, and a press that moves the element into it.                     |
| `.glass`        | Translucent surfaces over a blurred backdrop with a hairline highlight edge.                                                    |
| `.pixel`        | Corners cut by one grid unit, a chunky outline drawn as an inset ring, and the consumer-supplied `--font-pixel` over monospace. |
| `.chunky-tile`  | Rounded tiles seated on a darker bar of their own color, with a press that moves the element down into its own bar.             |
| `.cyber`        | Beveled corners, a thin bright edge, and a glow in the component's own color.                                                   |
| `.sketch`       | Varying elliptical corners, a solid ink line with dashed accents, a small offset shadow, and an optional handwriting face.      |

Aesthetics work with every fill and edge combination. `.ghost.edgeless` removes the fill and the border, so on a component whose aesthetic shows only through those and its shadow, little of the aesthetic is left; that is intended.

A presentation class on the element still wins over the aesthetic's defaults. The aesthetic sets how thick the border is; presentation decides whether it is drawn.

An aesthetic class on a component wins over one inherited from a container. This includes tooltip bubbles: `.tooltip-bubble.glass` gets the complete glass bubble under a pixel ancestor, and `.tooltip-bubble.pixel` gets the complete stepped bubble under a glass ancestor.

Your own CSS wins over an aesthetic. The aesthetic classes sit in the `components` cascade layer, so a rule in your own unlayered stylesheet beats them, and so does a Tailwind utility on the same element, such as `font-mono` on a `.pixel` region or `[--ui-radius:0]` on a `.cyber` one. See [Setup → Cascade layers](docs/setup.md#cascade-layers).

Most aesthetics scale from one number you can set, such as the offset of the neobrutalism shadow or the size of a pixel. These are the aesthetic's knobs, and each section below names its own. [Customizing → Aesthetic tokens](docs/usage/customizing.md#aesthetic-tokens) explains where they can be set.

To paint an aesthetic onto an element from another library, such as a toast or a dialog, use its [solo class](docs/usage/solo.md).

## Neobrutalism

The shadow is cast in the component's own intent, so a success button throws a green shadow and a destructive card a red one. With no intent, the outline and the shadow are the ink: near-black on a light page and near-white on a dark one. Fields and toggles are the exception. They draw the theme's control border, as they do with no aesthetic, because a resting checkbox outlined in near-black would look as loud as a checked one. The same holds under pixel, cyber, and sketch.

`--neo-offset` is the knob: the shadow offset and the distance the press travels are the same number, so scaling the look scales both at once.

```html
<section class="neobrutalism" style="--neo-offset: 6px">
  <button class="btn primary">A deeper shadow</button>
</section>
```

**Exceptions:**

- Content chips take the aesthetic too. A `.kbd` key cap's border changes from the quiet border gray to the ink, and from 1px to 2px, like every other border. A `.code` or `.pre` has no border by default, so it gets none; add `.edged` to give one an ink border.
- Only `.btn` and an opted-in `.card` respond to hover and press. A card opts in with `.interactive`, or with one of its halves — `.hoverable` for the hover response alone, `.pressable` for the press alone; a plain card, an alert, or a panel is a container and stays put.
- An alert sits on the offset shadow under this aesthetic, and under no other. An alert is otherwise flat, but here the shadow is a second outline rather than depth, and an alert without it looks unfinished next to everything else. This includes an alert inside a nested `.neobrutalism` region, and an alert that carries the class itself, `.alert.neobrutalism`. `.flat` still removes it and `.floating` still doubles it.
- The tooltip trigger takes the zero corner like everything else and draws square; `.radio` keeps its circle.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the press still happens, but at once: the element lands in its shadow without travelling there. The press is the feedback that a click registered, so only its motion goes.
- It has no font of its own and sets the theme's, `--font-default`, on the region, so a neobrutalist region nested inside pixel, cyber, sketch, or chunky tile does not take their face. A font you set with `font-family` alone, on `body` or a container, does not reach inside the region; set it in `--font-default` too, as [Theming → Fonts](docs/usage/theming.md#fonts) describes.

## Glass

`.glass` needs something behind it to blur. On a flat page background it renders as a plain translucent panel.

`--glass-radius` and `--glass-radius-surface` are the corners, at `0.75rem` and `1rem`. Glass is rounder than the base geometry because a translucent panel with a tight corner reads as a cut-out rather than as a pane.

```html
<section class="glass" style="--glass-radius-surface: 1.5rem">
  <div class="card">Softer</div>
</section>
```

**Exceptions:**

- Every surface in a glass region is glass, a neutral `.card.soft`, `.panel`, and `.alert` included.
- The glass is the ground, not the fill. A presentation keeps its whole fill, so a `.solid` button, a checked toggle, and a `.solid` card or table are opaque; the default, `.soft`, and `.ghost` panes are the frosted ones.
- The blur applies to `.card`, `.panel`, `.alert`, the tooltip bubble, and a default or `.soft` `.data-table` only. Controls stay solid and sit on the glass: a blur under every control of a dense cluster costs a composited layer apiece and reads as noise. Controls still take the aesthetic's radius, border, and shadow.
- Under `prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce`, and in forced colors, glass surfaces drop the blur and become opaque. Forced colors replace the colors but keep their transparency, so without this a pane would show the page through the system's background.
- Buttons and an opted-in `.card` press with the plain `scale(0.97)`; under reduced motion the press still happens, at once.
- It has no font of its own and sets the theme's, `--font-default`, on the region, as neobrutalism does.
- Text controls and toggles draw their line in the page's ink at 55% rather than the white hairline, which would erase an unchecked checkbox on a light page. It is `--ui-control-ink`; set it on the region to choose another.
- A table's frame and rules draw the page's ink at 20%, because the hairline vanishes on the table's plate. It is `--ui-rule-ink`.
- A table with a `<caption>` blurs behind the caption as well as its rows in Chromium and Safari, whose table box includes the caption, and under `.glass-liquid` the rim and sheen frame the caption too. Firefox keeps the caption off the pane. Label the table from a heading outside it with `aria-labelledby` where that matters.

### Liquid glass

`.glass-liquid` is a modifier of glass, after Apple's Liquid Glass: continuous corners, a bright rim where light catches the pane, a lighter blur, a clearer ground, and a lens that bends what is behind a surface at its edges. Put it beside `.glass` on the region, or on one surface inside a glass region.

```html
<section class="glass glass-liquid">
  <div class="card">A pane that bends the page behind it</div>
</section>
```

The lens is drawn by an SVG filter in `backdrop-filter`, which Chromium renders and Firefox and Safari do not yet. Elsewhere the pane keeps everything but the lens: the rim, the blur, the ground, and the corners, round rather than continuous where `corner-shape` is not drawn. Nothing needs to be in your markup: the filter ships inside the stylesheet.

**Exceptions:**

- It reaches `.card`, `.panel`, `.alert`, `.surface`, the tooltip bubble, a component of your own built with `@apply surface`, and a default or `.soft` `.data-table`. Controls stay solid, as they do under glass, except a button that asks: see [Liquid buttons](#liquid-buttons).
- It draws its blur and lens on each surface's `::before` and `::after`, so a surface inside a liquid region cannot carry a `::before` or `::after` of your own. Each surface also becomes a positioned stacking context; a surface you position yourself keeps your placement.
- Anything else that frosts under glass keeps liquid's light blur and its clearer ground, without the lens or the rim: a bare `<table>` under `/native`.
- The lens is 8px of erosion blurred over 10px on every surface, and 3px blurred over 3.5px on a button; its strength is fixed. A filter cannot read a custom property, so neither is a knob. The corners are, through `--glass-radius` and `--glass-radius-surface`, with larger defaults: a continuous corner reads smaller than a round one of the same radius.
- The nearest region decides. A region of another aesthetic nested inside a liquid region, or of plain `.glass`, keeps its own material and takes no layers, and a liquid region nested again inside that takes them back.
- Without `.glass` in scope it changes the corners and nothing else.
- Under `prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce`, and in forced colors, the blur and the lens go and the surface is opaque, as under glass.
- Text sits over a clearer pane than under glass. Over busy content, check that your text still reads: the ground is 30% of the page color, where glass's is 45%.

#### Liquid buttons

A button is a liquid pane when it carries `.glass-liquid` itself, inside a glass region. The modifier on the region alone leaves every button solid: a blur and a lens under each control of a dense toolbar cost two composited layers apiece and read as noise, so the one button that is meant to be glass says so.

```html
<section class="glass glass-liquid">
  <button class="btn primary">Solid, like every control</button>
  <button class="btn ghost glass-liquid">A clear pane</button>
  <button class="btn soft success glass-liquid">A tinted pane</button>
</section>
```

- The fill is still [presentation's](docs/usage/composing.md#presentation). `.ghost` is the clear pane and `.soft` the tinted one; a `.solid` button keeps its opaque plate and takes the rim and sheen over it. Intent, size, `.pill`, `.icon`, hover, and press all work as on any button.
- It works in a plain `.glass` region too, and on a button inside a liquid card.
- It spends the button's `::before` and `::after`, so a liquid button cannot carry one of your own.
- A disabled liquid button keeps the ground and the rim and loses the blur and the lens: it is dimmed with `opacity`, which cuts its layers off from the page behind it.
- The label sits over whatever is behind the button. Over busy content, check that it still reads, or use `.solid`.
- It reaches `.btn`, and a bare `<button>` only through its `.btn` class: the layers are a list of classes, which `/native`'s element mapping does not join.

## Pixel

`--pixel-unit` is one pixel of the imaginary low-resolution grid, `4px` by default. One square unit is cut from each corner and the outline is one unit thick, so the cut and what covers it are the same size.

```html
<section class="pixel" style="--pixel-unit: 6px">
  <button class="btn primary">Chunkier</button>
</section>
```

**Exceptions:**

- Corners are one unit or nothing. Small chips are square instead of stepped: badges, key caps, inline code, checkboxes, and switches. One unit off each corner of a 24px badge would look like a bite, not a corner.
- Surfaces are square too: a `.card`, `.panel`, or `.alert` keeps the inset ring but takes no cut and clips nothing. A clip would cut everything inside it, so a tooltip in a card, a shadow, or a focus ring there would be trimmed.
- Tables, progress bars, and skeletons are square too. A table takes no cut because in Chromium and WebKit its box includes its caption, and the cut would land on the caption instead of the rows. Progress bars and skeletons take only the square corner.
- A `.pre` code block is stepped like a button. It has no border by default, so the cut shows with no outline around it.
- The outline is an inset ring, because a clip removes a real border — and the focus ring, for the same reason, is a second inset layer rather than an outline. Both are the element's own edge rather than a shadow, so the border answers `.edged` and `.edgeless` the way a border does: a `.edgeless` badge and a `.solid` button draw none, a `.edged` card draws one, and a field keeps one whatever a container asks for.
- The inset focus ring carries a 2px line of the page color inside it. The ring is the primary color, so on a `.solid.primary` button it would be drawn over its own color; the line is what shows there.
- In forced colors the ring and the cut both go, because the system removes every box shadow: components draw a real 2px border and square corners, and `.pixel-solo` an inward outline.
- `.radio` and `.tooltip-icon` are never stepped. The circle is what tells a radio from a checkbox at a glance, so a radio stays round. A stepped 20px tooltip trigger would look bitten, so it is a plain square.
- `--font-pixel` is yours to supply. The package ships no font binary, so the aesthetic has no network side effect and falls back to the monospace stack.
- Whether digits are easy to read depends on the font you pick. At small sizes, such as page numbers, counters, and badges, some pixel fonts draw `2` and `8`, or `3` and `9`, so alike that they are misread. The CSS cannot fix that. Where small numbers matter, choose a font with clearly different digits.

## Chunky tile

Rounded tiles seated on a darker bar of their own color, pressed flat on click. The look mobile learning and game apps use; it is named for what it is made of rather than for any one product.

`--tile-lift` is how deep the bar is and how far a press travels, `4px` by default. One number drives both, so the top edge drops by exactly the bar's depth and the bottom edge does not move. `--tile-radius` is the corner, `0.75rem`, and it is one value rather than a control/surface pair on purpose — the shared corner is what makes a button and the card it sits in read as the same object.

```html
<section class="chunky-tile" style="--tile-lift: 6px; --tile-radius: 0.5rem">
  <button class="btn success">Continue</button>
</section>
```

The bar is a darker shade of the element's own color rather than a shadow under it, so it follows every intent: a success button sits on a dark green edge, a destructive one on a dark red edge, and a plain card on a gray edge that matches the line it already draws. Measured on the light palette, `.btn.success` is `#007a55` on `#004c34`. On a dark page a near-black surface cannot go darker, so its bar lands lighter and reads as a rim.

**Exceptions:**

- Only buttons and cards sit on a bar, because they are the components resting above zero elevation. A badge, chip, field, or tooltip is flat until it asks for depth with `.raised`, and `.flat` takes the bar off anything:

  ```html
  <div class="card soft edgeless info flat">Promo panel, deliberately flat</div>
  ```

- `--font-rounded` is yours to supply. A heavy rounded grotesque is most of this look and the package ships no font binary, so with nothing supplied the page's own stack is used.
- Labels are drawn heavier and slightly tracked, through `--ui-label-weight` and `--ui-label-tracking`, so your own `font-*` or `tracking-*` utility still wins. It reaches `.btn` and `.badge`, and a bare `<button>` only where `/native` styles it. Casing is left alone: how a label is worded is the application's decision, so if you want uppercase buttons, write that rule in your own stylesheet.
- `.card.interactive` presses like a `.btn`, so a chunky answer tile drops onto its bar on click; `.card.pressable` gets the same press on its own. A plain `.card` stays put.
- The shipped `.primary` is near-black on a light page and near-white on a dark one, and the bar is always mixed toward black. On a light page, a primary button's bar is almost invisible against its near-black face (measured `1.04:1`). On a dark page, the near-white face against the same bar reads well (`2.48:1`). Give `.primary` a hue of its own if it is the call to action and needs the depth cue in both themes.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the press still happens, but at once, as under neobrutalism.
- Depth in this aesthetic is the bar, never a blurred drop shadow. Anything that rests flat sits flush on the page.
- Controls draw a heavier gray than the tiles around them, `neutral-600` in light and `neutral-400` in dark, through `--ui-control-ink`, so a field reads as a field inside a tile.

## Cyber

Beveled corners, a 1px edge, and a glow in the component's own color: a success button glows green, a destructive card red. The bevel is drawn with `corner-shape`, so the border, the glow, and the focus outline all follow the cut rather than being clipped by it.

Controls and surfaces take the cut on opposite diagonals, so a button and the card around it read as the same material and as different things: buttons and fields cut top-left and bottom-right, cards, panels, and alerts top-right and bottom-left. Anything fully round cuts to points: a radio, a switch knob, and the tooltip icon become diamonds, and a pill button or a badge becomes a pointed hexagon. Chips go square, so the checkbox reads as a plain square beside the diamond radio.

`--cyber-cut` is the cut at the default size, `0.625rem`. Controls scale it with their size step, so a `.p-xs` icon button takes half of it and keeps its corners, and it stays a true 45 degrees. `--cyber-shape` and `--cyber-shape-surface` replace the default placement with any `border-radius` value, used as written. `--cyber-glow` is the glow's blur, `8px`. `--cyber-ink` is the neutral line and glow color. By default it follows the theme, near-black on a light page and near-white on a dark one; set it for a neon neutral.

```html
<section class="cyber" style="--cyber-ink: rgb(0 229 255); --cyber-cut: 0.75rem">
  <button class="btn">Open terminal</button>
</section>
```

Other shapes are a value away. Set them on the `.cyber` element or any ancestor. `--ui-radius` set on an element reaches that element and every component inside it that does not set its own. A shape you set is used as written and does not scale, so for a scaled one on a single control use `.cut-diagonal-reverse` instead.

| Shape                  | Value                 |
| ---------------------- | --------------------- |
| All four corners       | `0.625rem`            |
| The other diagonal     | `0 0.625rem`          |
| Hexagon (pointed ends) | `0.625rem / 50%`      |
| Parallelogram          | `0.625rem 0 / 100% 0` |
| One notch, top-right   | `0 0.625rem 0 0`      |

```html
<section class="cyber" style="--cyber-shape: 0.625rem / 50%">
  <button class="btn primary">Hexagonal buttons</button>
</section>
```

A parallelogram slants its sides into the content, so give a surface that takes one extra inline padding.

**Exceptions:**

- The bevel is Chromium-only today. Firefox and Safari do not draw `corner-shape` yet, and there the aesthetic squares its cut corners instead of rounding them, and what is fully round stays round, so the look degrades to square, lined, and glowing. It picks up the bevel with no change once an engine ships it.
- The glow is a halo, not depth, so every component takes it, fields, badges, and alerts included, and `.flat` does not take it off. `.raised` and `.floating` add no shadow under this aesthetic.
- In the light theme the glow of a neutral or `.primary` component is its near-black ink, which reads as a soft shadow rather than as light. The look is at its strongest on a dark page, or with a hued `--cyber-ink`.
- A plain `.btn.icon` is a square control, so it takes the control diagonal; a `.btn.icon.pill` is round, so it becomes a diamond.
- `--font-cyber` is yours to supply. The package ships no font binary, so the aesthetic falls back to the monospace stack.
- Casing is left alone, for the reason [Chunky tile](#chunky-tile) gives.

## Sketch

Hand-drawn outlines: controls take long, uneven elliptical corners, and cards, panels, alerts, and tables take sharper ones that stay clear of their padding. Siblings rotate through four outlines by position, and a field's control takes its field's position, so a row of buttons or a stacked form does not repeat one shape. The rotation is stable for a given DOM order, not random on each render. Every outline is a complete `border-radius`, used as written rather than scaled by the size step or placed by `.cut-diagonal`.

The 1px ink line is solid; checkboxes, dividers, and table rules are dashed. `--ui-line-style: dashed` dashes any other component, and `--ui-rule-style: solid` puts a divider or table back to solid. The 2px hard shadow is a small neutral depth cue.

`--sketch-radius`, `--sketch-radius-surface`, and `--sketch-radius-pill` replace the control, surface, and pill-button outlines. Set one on the region or on any element inside it, and every position below takes that one outline. To shape a single component instead, set `--ui-radius` (`--ui-radius-surface` on a surface) on it.

```html
<section class="sketch" style='--font-sketch: "Comic Sans MS", cursive'>
  <button class="btn primary">Send note</button>
  <button class="btn ghost edged" style="--ui-line-style: dashed">Draft note</button>
</section>
```

The dashed button is `ghost edged` because a filled button has no separate line to dash.

`.sketch-rounded` trades the long corners for short, rounded ones, bounded so a wide element keeps straight top and bottom edges. Put it beside `.sketch` on the region, or on one component inside it. `--sketch-radius-rounded` and `--sketch-radius-surface-rounded` are its knobs.

```html
<section class="sketch sketch-rounded">
  <div class="card">
    <button class="btn primary">Rounded action</button>
  </div>
</section>
```

**Exceptions:**

- Sketch names components to rotate their outlines, so its outlines reach only this package's components; a region of another aesthetic nested inside a sketch region keeps that aesthetic's corners. The nearest region decides, so a sketch region nested again inside that one rotates.
- Chips, such as checkboxes, key caps, code, badges, switches, and progress bars, rotate through small uneven outlines set in `--ui-radius-tight`. Set that token on a chip to choose its shape.
- A `.btn.pill` takes a rounded pill bounded to its own height, so a wide one does not become an oval. Badges, progress bars, and switches take their chip outline. Radios and the tooltip icon stay circles, slightly uneven, so a radio is never mistaken for a checkbox. An explicit `--ui-radius-pill` on an element still wins.
- `--font-sketch` is yours to supply. The package ships no handwriting font and falls back to the platform `cursive` family.
- Buttons press with the plain `scale(0.97)`; under reduced motion the press still happens, at once.
- With [`/native`](docs/setup.md#classless-html), a plain `<hr>`, `<table>`, and checkbox take the dashed accents of `.divider`, `.data-table`, and `.checkbox`.
- Forced-colors mode draws the dashed accents solid, like every other material line.

## Solo classes

An aesthetic class changes nothing on an element this package does not style, such as a toast from another library. Each aesthetic also ships a solo class, such as `.glass-solo`, that paints its look onto that one element. [Solo classes](docs/usage/solo.md) covers them.

## Next

[Solo classes](docs/usage/solo.md) applies these looks to components from other libraries. If every component on your screen comes from this package, the guides end here: [Composing](docs/usage/composing.md), [Customizing](docs/usage/customizing.md), and [Content and layout](docs/usage/content-and-layout.md) are the lookup pages, and [Accessibility](docs/accessibility.md) lists what your application still owes its users.

<!-- Source: docs/usage/solo.md -->

# Solo classes

Suppose the settings screen shows "Profile saved" in a toast from a notification library, not in this package's alert. Under `.neobrutalism`, every card and button has the thick outline and the hard shadow, and the toast does not: an aesthetic class only sets values that this package's components read, so it changes nothing on an element the package does not style. A solo class paints the aesthetic directly onto the one element that carries it:

```html
<div class="toast neobrutalism-solo success" role="status">Profile saved.</div>
```

## The six solo classes

Each aesthetic ships its solo class in the same entrypoint, and a solo class needs nothing else loaded:

```css
/* The only stylesheet from this package on the page. */
@import "@codenhub/styles/aesthetics/glass";
```

```html
<div class="toast glass-solo">A pane over whatever is behind it.</div>
```

| Aesthetic       | Solo class           | Paints                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.glass`        | `.glass-solo`        | A translucent background, a thin light edge, the blur, a soft two-layer shadow, and the surface corner. With `.glass-liquid`, the liquid pane, drawn on its `::before` and `::after`.                            |
| `.neobrutalism` | `.neobrutalism-solo` | A 2px ink edge, square corners, and the hard offset shadow.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `.pixel`        | `.pixel-solo`        | The stepped outline, the inner ring in place of a border, and the pixel font.                                                                                                                                    |
| `.chunky-tile`  | `.chunky-tile-solo`  | The tile corner, a 2px edge, the bar under it, and the rounded font.                                                                                                                                             |
| `.cyber`        | `.cyber-solo`        | The surface diagonal (the control diagonal on a button or link), a 1px edge, the glow, and the font.                                                                                                             |
| `.sketch`       | `.sketch-solo`       | Uneven elliptical corners (a sharper outline on a pane, a looser one on a button or link, and small rounded ones with `.sketch-rounded`), a 1px solid ink line, the 2px offset shadow, and the handwriting font. |

Do not put a solo class on this package's own components. A `.card` already draws its fill, edge, and intent, and a solo class would paint a second edge and fill over them. Use the aesthetic class there; it also works on a single element: `<button class="btn pixel">`.

## What a solo class reads

A solo element takes the same presentation, intent, and elevation classes a `.card` would:

```html
<div class="toast pixel-solo edgeless">No ring</div>
<div class="toast glass-solo solid success">An opaque green pane</div>
<div class="toast neobrutalism-solo flat">No offset shadow</div>

<section class="soft edged">
  <div class="toast chunky-tile-solo info">Soft and edged from the container, info from itself</div>
</section>
```

| What                                  | Read from                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Fill and edge (`.solid`, `.edged`, …) | The element, or any container: presentation passes down, as it does to components.                  |
| Intent (`.success`, …)                | The element only, as on components. A `.success` container leaves a solo element inside it neutral. |
| Elevation (`.flat`, `.raised`, …)     | The element only, as on components. It scales the offset shadow, the bar, and sketch's shadow.      |
| The aesthetic around it (`.pixel`, …) | Never. See [What a solo class ignores](#what-a-solo-class-ignores).                                 |

With none of those classes, a solo class paints the material alone (edge, corner, depth, outline, blur, font, and press) and leaves the element's own background and text color as they were.

- **Only the six built-in intents.** A solo class takes an intent from `.primary`, `.secondary`, `.success`, `.warning`, `.destructive`, and `.info` only. An intent class you defined yourself, as in [Theming → Your own intent](docs/usage/theming.md#your-own-intent), is not read, and the element is drawn neutral. To give a solo element a custom color, retheme one of the built-in intents on it or a container, as that section describes.
- **The fill is a layer over the element's own background.** Five of the six paint the fill as an inner shadow and do not set `background`, so a `.soft` solo toast is a tint over whatever the toast already was, and a `.solid` one with a colored intent is opaque. Glass sets its own background, because the translucent background is its material, and mixes the fill over it. A neutral `.solid` is a 20% tint, not the opaque gray a component draws.
- **The text color assumes the theme.** It is set only where a fill or an intent is asked for, and it is the color the theme uses on the page or on the fill. On an element whose own background does not follow the theme, such as a white toast on a dark page, a `.soft` or `.ghost` intent can put light text on a light background; use `.solid`, or leave the intent off.
- **There is no hover tint.** A solo element is not known to be clickable, so it does not get the hover color a `.btn` gets.
- **It reads its aesthetic's knobs and the theme's tokens, with the shipped values as fallbacks.** `--glass-radius-surface`, `--neo-offset`, `--pixel-unit`, `--tile-lift`, `--tile-radius`, `--cyber-cut`, `--cyber-shape`, `--cyber-shape-surface`, `--cyber-glow`, `--cyber-ink`, `--sketch-radius`, `--sketch-radius-surface`, `--sketch-radius-rounded`, `--sketch-radius-surface-rounded`, and the font tokens such as `--font-sketch` all work, set on the element or any ancestor. With the theme loaded, it follows the theme; without it, it renders the shipped look.
- **Dark values need a color scheme.** Light and dark pairs use `light-dark()`, which follows the element's `color-scheme`. The package's theme sets it; a page without the theme gets the light values.
- **The classes it reads come from the theme.** `.solid`, `.edgeless`, `.success`, `.flat`, and the rest ship in the base stylesheet and in `@codenhub/styles/theme`. With an aesthetic entrypoint alone on the page, those classes do nothing, and the solo class paints its unclassed look.

## What a solo class ignores

- **The aesthetic around it.** It reads none of the values an aesthetic class sets, and not `--elevation-color`. A `.glass-solo` inside a `.pixel` region keeps its own corners, and `--ui-radius` or `--ui-border-width` set on it or above it do nothing. Tune it through its knobs.
- **Its own children.** A solo element is not an aesthetic region. A component inside it keeps the look of the page around it, even with `.glass-liquid` or `.sketch-rounded` beside the solo class. It passes down only what any container does: the solo class's font, and the fill or edge of a presentation class on it, so a `.card` inside a `.glass-solo.solid` pane is solid, as inside any `.solid` container.
- **Glass's shadow and `.flat`.** `.flat` does not remove the shadow from `.glass-solo`, as it does not under `.glass`.

## How it wins and when it moves

- **It beats the other library's styles.** The rules are unlayered and one class deep, so they win over a component's layered rules, and over its zero-specificity ones, wherever the two load. An unlayered foreign rule that is more specific, or as specific and later in the page, still wins. The other side of this is that a Tailwind utility on the same element, such as `rounded-none`, loses to the solo class: tune it through its knobs instead.
- **It presses only an action.** Neobrutalism, chunky tile, and cyber press a `button`, `a[href]`, `[role="button"]`, `summary`, or button-type `input` that is not disabled by the `disabled` attribute, `.disabled`, `aria-disabled="true"`, or `data-disabled`, the four ways a button is disabled. Anything else stays put, so a toast does not sink when clicked. Chunky tile's heavier label follows the same rule.
- **It leaves a container's motion alone.** Only an action takes the press's `transition`, and the press moves the element through the `translate` and `scale` properties, not `transform`. A toast keeps its own transitions and its own `transform`. On an action, the press's `transition` replaces any the element had.
- **Reduced motion keeps the press and drops its motion.** Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, neobrutalism, chunky tile, and cyber still press, but at once: the element lands in its shadow or bar, or shrinks, without travelling there.

## Next

The guides end here. [Composing](docs/usage/composing.md), [Customizing](docs/usage/customizing.md), and [Content and layout](docs/usage/content-and-layout.md) are the lookup pages, and [Accessibility](docs/accessibility.md) lists what the CSS does for your users and what your application still owes them.

<!-- Source: docs/usage/composing.md -->

# Composing

This is a lookup page. [Building a screen](docs/concepts.md) introduces intent, presentation, and aesthetic; this page has the complete rules for combining them, the default look of every component, which classes each component reads, and elevation.

## Combining classes

```html
<div class="soft">
  <button class="btn primary">Soft primary button</button>
  <span class="badge success">Soft success badge</span>
  <button class="btn primary ghost edged">Outlined: the class on the element wins</button>
</div>
```

- **Presentation passes down.** `.solid`, `.soft`, `.ghost`, `.edged`, and `.edgeless` work on the component or on any container, and a class on the element beats one inherited from a container. A container sets the look of everything inside it, and any element can choose its own.
- **Aesthetics and [material tokens](docs/usage/customizing.md#material-tokens) pass down** the same way.
- **Intent does not pass down.** `.primary` and the other intent classes color only the element they are on. A container that silently recolored everything inside it would turn a red danger-zone card's neutral Cancel button red. `.neutral` names the default; use it where an element would otherwise take an intent, such as a table row inside a `.success` table. See [Theming → Intent tokens](docs/usage/theming.md#intent-tokens).
- **Elevation does not pass down.** `.raised` lifts only the element it is on; see [Elevation](#elevation).
- **Size does not pass down.** `.sm` and `.lg` resize only the button or control they are on, so a `.sm` form does not shrink the fields inside it. See [Buttons → Sizes and shapes](docs/usage/buttons.md#sizes-and-shapes) and [Forms → Sizes](docs/usage/forms.md#sizes).

With the Tailwind source entrypoints, every class above except the aesthetic classes is also a Tailwind utility, so variants such as `md:lg` and `dark:solid` work and `@apply btn primary soft sm` gives one class of yours the whole combination. The modifiers documented with each component, such as `.tight` or `.interactive`, are utilities too, so `@apply stack tight` works. The aesthetic classes, such as `.glass`, stay plain CSS, so `@apply glass` and `md:glass` do not work; write the class in the markup. See [Tailwind CSS v4 → Build your own components with `@apply`](docs/integrating/tailwind.md#build-your-own-components-with-apply), and [Presets](docs/usage/presets.md) for when to reach for it.

## Component defaults

With no presentation class on it or around it, each component has its own look. "Resting elevation" is how much depth it takes when an [aesthetic](docs/usage/aesthetics.md) draws depth; with no aesthetic, nothing has a shadow.

| Component                        | Fill        | Edge     | Resting elevation |
| -------------------------------- | ----------- | -------- | ----------------- |
| `.btn`                           | `.solid`    | edgeless | 1                 |
| `.card`                          | `.ghost`    | edged    | 1                 |
| `.panel`                         | `.soft`     | edgeless | 0                 |
| `.alert`                         | `.soft`     | edged    | 0                 |
| `.badge`                         | `.soft`     | edgeless | 0                 |
| `.ipt`, `.textarea`, `.select`   | `.ghost`    | edged    | 0                 |
| `.input-group`                   | `.ghost`    | edged    | 0                 |
| `.checkbox`, `.radio`, `.switch` | `.soft`     | edged    | 0                 |
| `.kbd`                           | `.soft`     | edged    | 0                 |
| `.code`, `.pre`                  | `.soft`     | edgeless | 0                 |
| `.data-table`                    | `.soft`     | edgeless | 0                 |
| `.progress` (the track)          | `.soft`     | edgeless | 0                 |
| `.tooltip-bubble`                | `.solid`    | edged    | 0                 |
| `.quote`                         | `.ghost`    | edged    | 0                 |
| `.skeleton`, `.divider`          | Intent only | None     | 0                 |

A neutral `.solid` fills only to 20%; see [Theming → Intent tokens](docs/usage/theming.md#intent-tokens). The neutral exceptions to these fills are in [Presentation](#presentation).

## Presentation

Presentation is two separate choices. `.solid`, `.soft`, and `.ghost` set how much of the intent color fills a component. `.edged` and `.edgeless` set whether it draws a border. They set [presentation tokens](docs/usage/customizing.md#presentation-tokens) and nothing else.

| Class       | Look                                                      | `--ui-fill` | `--ui-fg-on-fill` | `--ui-border` |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------- | ------------- |
| `.solid`    | Filled with the intent color, with contrast text.         | `100%`      | `100%`            |               |
| `.soft`     | A light tint, with intent-colored text.                   | `12%`       | `0%`              |               |
| `.ghost`    | No fill at rest, with intent-colored text.                | `0%`        | `0%`              |               |
| `.edged`    | An intent-colored border, as thick as the aesthetic sets. |             |                   | `100%`        |
| `.edgeless` | No border.                                                |             |                   | `0%`          |

```html
<button class="btn primary">Solid, the button default</button>
<button class="btn soft edged">Tinted, with a border</button>
<button class="btn primary ghost edged">Outline</button>
<button class="btn ghost">Ghost: picks up a tint on hover</button>
<input class="ipt soft edgeless" aria-label="Search" />
```

A fill class never sets the border, and a border class never sets the fill. `.solid.edged` looks the same as `.solid.edgeless`, because the border fades out as the fill fills in.

The border is the outline of the component and nothing else. Lines inside a component, such as the rules between table rows, are a separate switch; see [Content and layout → Table rules](docs/usage/content-and-layout.md#table-rules).

### Neutral surfaces rest untinted

A neutral `.card.soft`, `.panel`, and `.alert` show no tint at rest. They use the quiet background tone one step off the page instead (`--color-foreground`), because a gray tint on every neutral box looks dirty rather than quiet.

- A `.card.soft` with `.interactive` or `.hoverable` shows the tint on hover. A plain `.card.soft` and a `.panel` have no hover state.
- With one of the six built-in intents, all three keep the ordinary 12% tint, and a card deepens it on hover. An intent you defined yourself is treated as neutral here; see [Theming → Your own intent](docs/usage/theming.md#your-own-intent).
- The presentation can come from the element or from a container: `<div class="soft"><div class="card">` rests like `.card.soft`, and a `.ghost` or `.solid` container gives a `.panel` or `.alert` the plate its own class would.
- A `.badge` keeps its 12% tint even when neutral. It has no border, so without the tint it would disappear into the text around it.

`.kbd`, `.code`, and `.pre` work differently. They rest on their intent's subtle tone, `--intent-subtle`, which is `--color-surface` for neutral, and a built-in intent adds 12% of its color over it. An intent you defined yourself shows its own `--intent-subtle` tint without that extra 12%.

### Text controls and toggles

- **Text controls** cap their fill so typed text stays readable: at most 6% from a container, 12% for their own `.soft`, and 20% for their own `.solid`. They ignore an `.edgeless` from a container and honor their own. See [Forms → Fill and border on text controls](docs/usage/forms.md#fill-and-border-on-text-controls).
- **Toggles** cap their unchecked fill at 40% and fill to 100% once checked. `.checkbox` and `.radio` always draw their border, and so does `.switch.ghost`. See [Forms → Checked and unchecked colors](docs/usage/forms.md#checked-and-unchecked-colors).

### Tooltip bubbles

A tooltip bubble is always filled and opaque, and draws a thin border that only its own `.edgeless` removes. With no intent it uses `--color-tooltip`; an intent fills it with that intent's color. [Tooltips → How the bubble looks](docs/usage/tooltips.md#how-the-bubble-looks) has the colors.

### Progress tracks

`.progress` reads both choices on its track. The filled part is always the intent color at full strength. `.solid` is not supported on the track, because the track and the filled part would be the same color. `.ghost.edgeless` renders but leaves the track with no visible frame; `.ghost.edged` draws an outline around it.

### Unsupported combinations

| Component               | Class       | What happens                                                                                 |
| ----------------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.kbd`, `.code`, `.pre` | `.ghost`    | The chip still draws its tinted background, because that background is what makes it a chip. |
| `.progress`             | `.solid`    | The track and the filled part are the same color, so the value cannot be seen.               |
| `.checkbox`, `.radio`   | `.edgeless` | Ignored: the border is always drawn.                                                         |

## Component axis reference

Which classes change each component. "Material" is what an [aesthetic](docs/usage/aesthetics.md) can change on it: "Shape" means corner, border width, shadow, hover, and outline; the narrower entries list what applies.

| Components                                                | Intent | Fill | Edge | Material           |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ---- | ---- | ------------------ |
| `.btn`, `.alert`, `.badge`, `.card`, `.panel`             | Yes    | Yes  | Yes  | Shape              |
| `.kbd`, `.data-table`                                     | Yes    | Yes  | Yes  | Corner and edge    |
| `.quote`                                                  | Yes    | Yes  | Yes  | Edge width         |
| `.divider`, `.skeleton`                                   | Yes    | No   | No   | No                 |
| `.ipt`, `.textarea`, `.select`, `.text-control`           | Yes    | Yes  | Yes  | Shape              |
| `.input-group`                                            | Yes    | Yes  | Yes  | Shape              |
| `.surface`                                                | Yes    | Yes  | Yes  | Shape              |
| `.checkbox`, `.radio`                                     | Yes    | Yes  | No   | Corner and edge    |
| `.switch`                                                 | Yes    | Yes  | Yes  | Corner and edge    |
| `.progress`                                               | Yes    | Yes  | Yes  | Corner and edge    |
| `.code`, `.pre`                                           | Yes    | Yes  | Yes  | Corner and outline |
| `.tooltip-bubble`                                         | Yes    | Yes  | Yes  | Shape and blur     |
| `.table-wrap`, `.quote-inline`, layout and text utilities | No     | No   | No   | No                 |

"Yes" means the class changes the component, and "No" means it does not; the package's tests check both. What each component does with a class:

| Component                                       | Reads                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.btn`, `.alert`, `.badge`, `.card`, `.panel`   | Fill, text color, border, and border width.                                            |
| `.kbd`                                          | Fill, text color, border, and border width.                                            |
| `.data-table`                                   | Header fill and text color, border, and border width.                                  |
| `.ipt`, `.textarea`, `.select`, `.text-control` | Border, border width, and a capped fill.                                               |
| `.input-group`                                  | Border, border width, and a capped fill.                                               |
| `.checkbox`, `.radio`                           | A capped fill, checked and unchecked.                                                  |
| `.switch`                                       | Border, border width, and a capped fill.                                               |
| `.quote`                                        | Fill, text color, border, and border width.                                            |
| `.code`, `.pre`, `.tooltip-bubble`              | Fill, text color, border, and material.                                                |
| `.progress`                                     | Track fill, border, and border width. The filled part is always the full intent color. |
| `.skeleton`, `.divider`                         | Intent only.                                                                           |

State and modifier classes such as `.interactive`, `.hoverable`, `.pressable`, `.p-sm`, and `.vertical` are documented with their component. Each takes effect on the components that read it, and on `/tw` they are utilities, so `@apply card interactive` works. An invalid control is marked with `aria-invalid="true"`, not a class; see [Forms](docs/usage/forms.md#show-a-validation-error).

## Elevation

Elevation is how much depth a component takes. Nothing has a shadow until an [aesthetic](docs/usage/aesthetics.md) draws depth or one of these classes asks for it.

| Class       | Depth                                                                                |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `.flat`     | None. Glass surfaces keep their shadow, because it is part of what glass is made of. |
| `.raised`   | One step of the depth in scope: cards and tiles that sit close to the page.          |
| `.floating` | Two steps: menus and popovers.                                                       |

```html
<article class="card raised">Lifted</article>
<div class="floating panel">A menu</div>
<article class="card flat">Flat, whatever the aesthetic says</article>
```

Each class multiplies the shadow of the aesthetic in scope. The same `.raised` is a soft blur on a plain page and a hard offset shadow under `.neobrutalism`: the aesthetic decides what depth looks like, and the class decides how much of it this element takes.

The class does not pass down. It lifts or flattens only the element it is on, and an element inside it takes no depth from it. Give each element that needs depth its own class. The spread of a shadow is not multiplied, because an aesthetic that draws its border as an inner shadow uses the spread for that border.

These classes are separate from the `--elevation-*` shadow tokens in [Theming → Foundation tokens](docs/usage/theming.md#foundation-tokens), which are fixed shadows for elements you style yourself.

<!-- Source: docs/usage/customizing.md -->

# Customizing

This is a lookup page for changing the package beyond its classes. [Theming](docs/usage/theming.md) covers colors and the foundation tokens; this page covers the rest:

- [Presentation tokens](#presentation-tokens): how much of an intent a component shows.
- [Material tokens](#material-tokens): what a component is made of.
- [Aesthetic tokens](#aesthetic-tokens): the knobs each aesthetic exposes.
- [Component variables](#component-variables): the six variables a single component reads.
- [Generated palette](#generated-palette): fixed color values for code that cannot load the package.
- [Composition helpers](#composition-helpers): the classes to build a component of your own from.

## Presentation tokens

Presentation tokens describe _how much_ of an intent a component shows, never _which_ intent it shows. They are unitless numbers and percentages, so they carry no color and inherit safely: a container sets them once and every component below resolves them against its own intent.

| Token             | Purpose                                                                                             | Default                             |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `--ui-fill`       | Percentage of the intent color mixed into the background.                                           | The component's default; see below. |
| `--ui-fg-on-fill` | Percentage blended from the intent's strong tone toward its contrast color.                         | The component's default.            |
| `--ui-border`     | Percentage of the intent's border color in the border.                                              | The component's default.            |
| `--hover-step`    | Added to the resting fill under the pointer, in `--intent-hover`. Set it on `:root` or any element. | `14%`                               |

Unset, each component uses its own default, listed in [Composing → Component defaults](docs/usage/composing.md#component-defaults). The presentation classes set the first three to the values in [Composing → Presentation](docs/usage/composing.md#presentation). There are no hover tokens per presentation: hover is always the resting fill plus `--hover-step`, up to 100%.

No fill class writes `--ui-border` and no edge class writes `--ui-fill`. A filled box with no line is `.solid.edgeless`, and `.solid.edged` renders the same box: the line fades out as the fill fills in, so even a neutral fill, capped and translucent, shows through its own border as one coat.

```css
background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-primary) var(--ui-fill, 100%), transparent);
```

Two choices there are deliberate. Mixing toward `transparent` rather than a background token lets a tinted surface adapt to whatever it is placed on. Mixing in `oklab` keeps the wide-gamut token palette intact and blends perceptually, where `srgb` would clip it.

A computed color therefore reaches the page as a resolved `color-mix` result rather than the token's own `oklch` syntax. It is the same color; code that compares computed color strings should compare colors instead.

> **Presentation token contract**: only presentation classes and consumer overrides set these tokens; components only read them. Setting a value that no presentation class produces is supported but unvalidated. See [Composing](docs/usage/composing.md) for the classes that ship these values.

## Material tokens

Material tokens describe what a component is _made of_ rather than which intent it shows or how strongly. They control shape, borders, shadows, translucency, filters, and transforms.

Components read each with a fallback, so leaving them unset gives the default look. Set on a container, they restyle everything inside it. The one exception is `--ui-elevation`, which does not inherit, so it reaches only the element it is set on; see [Composing → Elevation](docs/usage/composing.md#elevation).

Shadow geometry is split into parts with no color in them, so they inherit safely. Tokens that take a color, such as `--ui-ink` and `--ui-surface-shadow`, may include their own.

| Token                     | Purpose                                                                                                                                              | Fallback                                  |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `--ui-corner`             | Control corner at the default size; scaled by the size step.                                                                                         | `--radius-control`                        |
| `--ui-corner-surface`     | Surface corner at the default padding; scaled by the size step.                                                                                      | `--radius-surface`                        |
| `--ui-corner-tl`          | `0` or `1`: whether the top-left takes the corner. `-tr`, `-br`, and `-bl` for the others.                                                           | `1`                                       |
| `--ui-radius`             | A complete control radius, used as written: overrides the corner, the step, and the pattern.                                                         | Computed from the corner                  |
| `--ui-radius-surface`     | A complete surface radius, used as written.                                                                                                          | Computed from the corner                  |
| `--ui-scale`              | Overrides the size step the size and padding classes set.                                                                                            | The step                                  |
| `--ui-corner-shape`       | What every corner draws: `round`, `bevel` for a straight cut, or `squircle` for a continuous curve. Chromium only today.                             | `round`                                   |
| `--ui-radius-pill`        | Corner for what is fully round by default: badges, switches, progress, the tooltip icon; `.btn.pill` and `.radio` read it with no fallback but full. | `--ui-radius`, `--ui-corner`, then full   |
| `--ui-radius-tight`       | Complete radius for chips, such as a checkbox, `.kbd`, or `.code`, when set. Unset, a small computed default.                                        | `min(--ui-radius or --ui-corner, small)`  |
| `--ui-line-style`         | Style of every line a component draws: `solid`, `dashed`, `dotted`, or `double` (3px wide or more).                                                  | `solid`                                   |
| `--ui-border-width`       | Edge thickness.                                                                                                                                      | `--border-width`                          |
| `--ui-border-max`         | Ceiling on computed edge width.                                                                                                                      | `100px`                                   |
| `--ui-ink`                | Neutral line color when no intent is set.                                                                                                            | `--color-border`                          |
| `--ui-control-ink`        | Neutral line color of fields, selects, checkboxes, radios, and switches when no intent is set.                                                       | `--ui-ink`, then `--color-control-border` |
| `--ui-rule-ink`           | Neutral line color of a table's frame and rules when no intent is set.                                                                               | `--ui-ink`, then `--color-border`         |
| `--ui-rule`               | Lines inside a table. Unset draws the head and foot boundaries only; `0%` draws none; `100%` rules every row.                                        | unset                                     |
| `--ui-shadow-x`           | Shadow horizontal offset.                                                                                                                            | `0px`                                     |
| `--ui-shadow-y`           | Shadow vertical offset.                                                                                                                              | `0px`                                     |
| `--ui-shadow-blur`        | Shadow blur radius.                                                                                                                                  | `0px`                                     |
| `--ui-shadow-spread`      | Shadow spread radius.                                                                                                                                | `0px`                                     |
| `--ui-shadow-inset`       | The `inset` keyword for an inner ring.                                                                                                               | Empty                                     |
| `--ui-hover-shadow-x`     | Shadow horizontal offset while hovered.                                                                                                              | `--ui-shadow-x`                           |
| `--ui-hover-shadow-y`     | Shadow vertical offset while hovered.                                                                                                                | `--ui-shadow-y`                           |
| `--ui-active-shadow-x`    | Shadow horizontal offset while pressed.                                                                                                              | `--ui-shadow-x`                           |
| `--ui-active-shadow-y`    | Shadow vertical offset while pressed.                                                                                                                | `--ui-shadow-y`                           |
| `--ui-active-transform`   | Transform while pressed. Kept under `prefers-reduced-motion`, which drops only its transition.                                                       | `scale(0.97)`                             |
| `--ui-active-translate-x` | Distance a press travels into the element's depth; `-y` beside it. Scaled like the shadow.                                                           | `0px`                                     |
| `--ui-shadow-ink`         | Percentage of shadow color taken from intent ink.                                                                                                    | `0%`                                      |
| `--ui-halo-blur`          | Blur of a halo around the element; `--ui-halo-spread` beside it. Elevation does not scale it.                                                        | `0px`                                     |
| `--ui-halo-ink`           | The halo's share of the intent color, over nothing. Unset, there is no halo.                                                                         | Unset                                     |
| `--ui-shadow-edge`        | Declared, even empty, when the shadow is the element's edge rather than its depth. Read for presence.                                                | Unset                                     |
| `--ui-elevation`          | Unitless multiplier over shadow geometry. Does not inherit.                                                                                          | `1`                                       |
| `--ui-surface-shadow`     | Complete multi-layer shadow accepted by surfaces only.                                                                                               | Unset                                     |
| `--ui-surface-ground`     | Ground a surface, or a default or `.soft` table, sits on.                                                                                            | `--color-background`                      |
| `--ui-bg-alpha`           | Multiplier over every fill, `.solid` included. No shipped aesthetic sets it.                                                                         | `1`                                       |
| `--ui-backdrop`           | Backdrop filter accepted by surfaces, and by a default or `.soft` table, only.                                                                       | `none`                                    |
| `--ui-surface-image`      | A painted layer over a surface's plate: any `background-image` value. Surfaces only.                                                                 | `none`                                    |
| `--ui-hover-transform`    | Transform while an interactive element is hovered.                                                                                                   | `none`                                    |
| `--ui-clip`               | Structural component silhouette.                                                                                                                     | `none`                                    |
| `--ui-clip-tight`         | Compact component silhouette.                                                                                                                        | `--ui-clip`                               |
| `--ui-focus-inset`        | Inset focus layer width.                                                                                                                             | Unset                                     |
| `--ui-label-weight`       | Label weight of `.btn` (and, with `/native`, a bare `<button>`) and `.badge`.                                                                        | Semibold on a button, bold on a badge     |
| `--ui-label-tracking`     | Label letter spacing. Unset, it is `normal`, so neither the page's tracking nor a container's reaches the label.                                     | `normal`                                  |
