| `--ui-label-case`         | Label `text-transform`.                                                                                                                              | `none` on a button; inherited on a badge  |
| `--ui-label-shadow`       | Label `text-shadow`, written without a color so it takes the label's own.                                                                            | `none` on a button; inherited on a badge  |

```html
<section style="--ui-corner: 0; --ui-border-width: 3px">
  <button class="btn primary">Square and heavy</button>
  <input class="ipt" placeholder="Matches" />
</section>
```

> **Material token contract**: components read these; aesthetic classes and consumer overrides set them.

### Corner size and pattern

The corner scales with the element. `.p-xs` sets a size step of `0.5`, `.sm` and `.p-sm` `0.75`, and `.lg` and `.p-lg` `1.25`. When a size class and a padding class sit on one element, the smaller step wins, so `.lg.p-xs` is small. `box` multiplies `--ui-corner` by the step, so a small button takes a small corner and a bevel stays a true 45 degrees. Depth follows the step down but not up: a `.p-xs` button sits on half its aesthetic's shadow, and a `.lg` one on the whole of it. A press that travels into that depth, given as `--ui-active-translate-x` and `-y`, travels the same scaled distance, so it always lands flat.

Which corners take the corner is its own choice. `.cut-diagonal` keeps the top-left and bottom-right and squares the other two; `.cut-diagonal-reverse` keeps the other pair. Both set `--ui-corner-tl`, `-tr`, `-br`, and `-bl`, which you can also set yourself: a two-corner leaf on the default look, two cuts on a control under `.cyber`. A surface under `.cyber` keeps the aesthetic's own surface shape, which the pattern does not reach, and an explicit `--ui-radius` or `--ui-radius-surface` ignores the step and the pattern.

### Lines, layers, and labels

`--ui-line-style` reaches every line a component draws: the box's edge, the progress track, and dividers and table rules. `--ui-rule-style` optionally overrides just dividers and table rules, without changing the box edge; sketch uses it for dashed accents. A dashed or dotted line keeps its color, so it keeps its contrast. A `double` line needs a width of 3px or more to draw two lines.

`--ui-halo-*` is light rather than depth: a glow in the element's own intent color. Elevation does not scale it, and `.flat` leaves it on. It appears only when its ink is set.

`--ui-surface-image` lays any `background-image` over a surface's plate: cards, panels, alerts, and tooltips, not controls. Whoever sets it owns the contrast of the text over it, and your own `background-image` on a surface still wins.

`--ui-label-*` treats the label of a button or a badge: weight, tracking, case, and a text shadow. Write the shadow without a color, such as `0 0 6px`, so it takes the label's own color and cannot lower its contrast. Your own `font-*`, `tracking-*`, and case utilities still win. A label does not inherit tracking, so a `tracking-*` utility on a container leaves its buttons and badges at `normal`; to track every label in a region, set `--ui-label-tracking` on it, which they inherit.

Under forced colors each of these draws its plain version: a solid line, no halo, no painted layer, and no label shadow. The silhouette and the ring below go too. Forced colors remove every box shadow, so `--ui-clip`, `--ui-clip-tight`, `--ui-border-max`, and `--ui-shadow-edge` are cleared and a component draws its real border at `--ui-border-width`.

### Shape and ring composition

Clipping removes borders, outlines, and outer shadows. An aesthetic that uses a clip can replace the border with an inset shadow by setting `--ui-shadow-inset` and the four shadow geometry parts. Set `--ui-border-max: 0px` when that ring replaces the component border. Focusable components restore the clipped focus outline through `--ui-focus-inset`: an inset layer of that width in `--focus-ring`, with a 2px line of `--color-background` inside it so focus still shows on a component filled with the ring's own color.

A clip is not the only way to cut a corner. `--ui-corner-shape: bevel` draws the corner the radius sets as a straight cut instead of an arc, and the border, outer shadow, focus outline, and backdrop all follow it. A beveled element therefore keeps its glow and its line, where a clipped one loses both. `.cyber` uses it. Engines without `corner-shape` ignore it and draw the radius round, so an aesthetic that bevels should square its radius under `@supports not (corner-shape: bevel)`. A bevel on a full radius cuts to points: a radio, a `.btn.pill`, and anything reading `--ui-radius-pill` become diamonds or pointed hexagons.

`--ui-radius` accepts any `border-radius` value and is used as written, so it can place the corner per side: `10px 0` cuts only top-left and bottom-right. The pill and chip corners are separate tokens. An unset chip corner computes a small default from `--ui-radius`, then `--ui-corner`, capped at `--radius-small`; an explicit `--ui-radius-tight` is used as written, even for a per-corner or elliptical value. Aesthetic and consumer overrides can therefore give a chip a larger or more irregular shape. `.btn.pill` takes `--ui-radius-pill` ahead of the other radii; under sketch it takes an uneven hand-drawn pill outline whose ends stay the same size. An explicit `--ui-radius-pill` on that button still wins.

Declare `--ui-shadow-edge` when that ring _is_ the border. The ring then takes the element's edge color, which carries the edge axis as its alpha, so `.edged` draws it and `.edgeless` does not — the same answer a real border gives. Without it the ring paints on every component the aesthetic reaches and the edge classes have no effect. Use `--ui-shadow-ink` instead when the shadow is depth cast in the intent's own ink, such as a hard offset slab, which an `.edgeless` element still gets.

The token is read for its presence, not its value: declare it empty to switch the ring on, and `initial` to switch it back off in an aesthetic nested inside one that declares it.

```css
.stepped {
  --ui-clip: polygon(/* structural silhouette */);
  --ui-clip-tight: none;
  --ui-border-max: 0px;
  --ui-shadow-inset: inset;
  --ui-shadow-edge: ;
  --ui-shadow-x: 0px;
  --ui-shadow-y: 0px;
  --ui-shadow-blur: 0px;
  --ui-shadow-spread: 4px;
  --ui-focus-inset: var(--focus-ring-width);
}
```

Variables prefixed `--_` are internal composition outputs — `--_bg`, `--_fg`, `--_edge`, `--_fill`, `--_shadow`, and the `--_d-*` resting slots a component states for `box` to read. Do not set or read them; only the `--ui-*` inputs above are public.

## Aesthetic tokens

The shipped [aesthetic classes](docs/usage/aesthetics.md) set material tokens for you. Only aesthetics with a token listed below expose an aesthetic-specific token. Tune all other behavior through the shared material tokens above. Listed tokens are available only where that aesthetic's stylesheet is imported.

| Token                             | Aesthetic                    | Purpose                                                                                         | Default                                                            |
| --------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--neo-offset`                    | `.neobrutalism`              | Hard shadow offset and distance the press travels.                                              | `4px`                                                              |
| `--glass-radius`                  | `.glass`, `.glass-liquid`    | Control corner radius. `1rem` under `.glass-liquid`.                                            | `0.75rem`                                                          |
| `--glass-radius-surface`          | `.glass`, `.glass-liquid`    | Surface corner radius. `1.5rem` under `.glass-liquid`.                                          | `1rem`                                                             |
| `--pixel-unit`                    | `.pixel`                     | One pixel of the grid. The corner cut and the ring are one.                                     | `4px`                                                              |
| `--font-pixel`                    | `.pixel`                     | Consumer-supplied pixel font stack.                                                             | Falls back to the monospace stack                                  |
| `--tile-radius`                   | `.chunky-tile`               | Corner radius, on controls and surfaces alike.                                                  | `0.75rem`                                                          |
| `--tile-lift`                     | `.chunky-tile`               | Depth of the seated bar, and how far a press travels.                                           | `4px`                                                              |
| `--font-rounded`                  | `.chunky-tile`               | Consumer-supplied rounded font stack.                                                           | Falls back to the page stack                                       |
| `--cyber-cut`                     | `.cyber`                     | The cut at the default size, on controls and surfaces alike; controls scale it with the step.   | `0.625rem`                                                         |
| `--cyber-shape`                   | `.cyber`                     | Where controls take the cut: any `border-radius` value.                                         | `<cut> 0` (top-left, bottom-right)                                 |
| `--cyber-shape-surface`           | `.cyber`                     | Where surfaces take the cut: any `border-radius` value.                                         | `0 <cut>` (top-right, bottom-left)                                 |
| `--cyber-glow`                    | `.cyber`                     | Blur of the glow.                                                                               | `8px`                                                              |
| `--cyber-ink`                     | `.cyber`                     | Neutral line and glow color, where no intent sets one.                                          | Theme ink (near-black, near-white)                                 |
| `--font-cyber`                    | `.cyber`                     | Consumer-supplied technical font stack.                                                         | Falls back to the monospace stack                                  |
| `--sketch-radius`                 | `.sketch`                    | Control outline radius: any `border-radius` value.                                              | Irregular box outline with sibling variation                       |
| `--sketch-radius-surface`         | `.sketch`                    | Surface container outline radius: any `border-radius` value.                                    | Sharp irregular square outline with sibling variation              |
| `--sketch-radius-rounded`         | `.sketch`, `.sketch-rounded` | Rounded control outline radius: expressive elliptical contour with sibling variation.           | `26px 10px 24px 11px / 12px 23px 11px 20px` with sibling variation |
| `--sketch-radius-surface-rounded` | `.sketch`, `.sketch-rounded` | Rounded surface container outline radius: expressive elliptical contour with sibling variation. | `38px 16px 36px 17px / 16px 34px 17px 32px` with sibling variation |
| `--sketch-radius-pill`            | `.sketch`                    | Radius of a pill button's outline: an uneven hand-drawn pill whose ends stay the same size.     | `24px 16px 23px 17px / 17px 21px 16px 20px` with sibling variation |
| `--font-sketch`                   | `.sketch`                    | Consumer-supplied handwriting font stack.                                                       | Falls back to `cursive`                                            |

Every aesthetic's knobs reach the same way: each knob is _read_ with its default as a `var()` fallback rather than declared, so it resolves once into a private on the aesthetic's own class (`--_pixel-unit`, `--_neo-offset`, `--_tile-radius`, `--_tile-lift`, and so on). Set a knob on the element carrying the aesthetic class, or on any ancestor including `:root`:

```html
<section class="pixel" style="--pixel-unit: 6px">
  <button class="btn primary">Chunkier</button>
</section>
```

```html
<html class="pixel" style="--pixel-unit: 6px">
  <body>
    <button class="btn primary">Also chunkier, set from the root</button>
  </body>
</html>
```

Knobs and material tokens reach in opposite directions. A knob is read once, at the element with the aesthetic class, and the result passes down. So set a knob on that element or on one above it; set on an element inside the aesthetic, it changes nothing, because the value has already been read.

`--ui-radius`, `--ui-radius-surface`, and the other material tokens are read by each component as it draws. They work on the element they are set on and everything inside it, which is how you round one card differently from its neighbors without touching the knob. Mind which one a component reads: a surface (`.card`, `.panel`, `.alert`) takes `--ui-radius-surface`, and a control such as `.btn` or `.ipt` takes `--ui-radius`. `style="--ui-radius-surface: 0"` squares one card; `--ui-radius` on that card squares the buttons inside it and leaves the card round.

Shipped aesthetics set the shared material tokens above. Every shipped aesthetic sets `--ui-ink` for its neutral line. Every shipped aesthetic also sets `--ui-control-ink`: `.glass` and `.chunky-tile` to a line of their own, heavier than their surfaces', and the others to `--color-control-border`, since their ink is near-black or near-white and a resting checkbox outlined in it would look checked. `.glass` sets `--ui-rule-ink` too, so a table's lines read on its plate; the others clear it. Intent classes still override the intent slots on each component.

The same knobs tune each aesthetic's [solo class](docs/usage/solo.md), which reads them on its own element.

## Generated palette

`@codenhub/styles/palette` is a generated stylesheet of fixed colors: for every intent and presentation, the background, text, and border color a component would draw, as flat `--palette-*` custom properties. It is for code that cannot load this package's stylesheet, such as a library that lists `@codenhub/styles` as an optional peer, but wants to match it. Where you can load the stylesheet, use the components instead.

**The values are a snapshot of the shipped colors.** They were computed from the package's default theme when it was built, and they do not change when you override a token. If you set `--color-primary` to your brand color, `--palette-primary-solid-bg` is still the shipped near-black. Code that must follow your theme has to read the `--color-*` tokens, which means loading `@codenhub/styles/theme`.

```css
@import "@codenhub/styles/palette";
```

```css
.my-badge {
  background: var(--palette-success-soft-bg);
  color: var(--palette-success-soft-fg);
  border-color: var(--palette-success-soft-edge);
}
```

Every value is a finished color, never a reference to another variable, so the file needs nothing else loaded.

Naming: `--palette-<intent>-<presentation>-<slot>`, where `<intent>` is one of the seven published intents (`neutral`, `primary`, `secondary`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`, `info`) and `<presentation>` is `solid`, `soft`, or `ghost`. `<slot>` is `bg`, `fg`, or `edge`. Two qualifiers layer on only where they apply:

- A ground qualifier, `page` or `subtle`, before the slot. It appears only on the `bg` and `edge` of `.soft` and `.ghost`, because a `.solid` fill covers its ground and the text color never depends on it.
  - No qualifier is what `.badge` and `.btn` draw, on a transparent ground: `--palette-success-soft-bg`.
  - `page` is what `.alert` draws, on the page: `--palette-success-soft-page-bg`.
  - `subtle` is what `.kbd`, `.code`, and `.pre` draw, on the intent's own subtle tone: `--palette-success-soft-subtle-bg`.

  Each value is read from the component itself, so it includes what the component does on its own. A neutral `.alert`, `.kbd`, `.code`, or `.pre` keeps a quieter fill than a neutral `.badge`, and its `neutral-soft-page` and `neutral-soft-subtle` values say so. `.tooltip-bubble` matches none of the three: with no intent it fills with its own tooltip tone, and its edge is solid rather than faded.

- A `-hover` suffix, on `bg` and `edge` only, because the text color does not change on hover: `--palette-success-soft-page-bg-hover`. `.alert`, `.kbd`, `.code`, and `.pre` have no hover of their own, so their hover values are what the component draws when you add `box-hover` to it.

Light values are set on `:root`. Dark values apply under `.dark`, `.theme-dark`, or `[data-theme="dark"]` on the element or an element above it, the same selectors the package's theme uses. The light values also apply under `.light`, `.theme-light`, and `[data-theme="light"]`, so the nearest explicit theme wins: a light area inside a dark one reads the light values.

The file does not follow `prefers-color-scheme`. Code that uses the palette on its own already switches themes itself, so it sets one of those classes or attributes.

Nor does it follow `prefers-contrast: more`. Under that setting the package draws each intent's border in its strong tone, so a `-edge` value is fainter than the border the component draws. Code that has to honor the setting picks a stronger color itself.

Three more tokens have no intent, presentation, ground, or hover: `--palette-border`, `--palette-surface`, and `--palette-text`, fixed values of `--color-border`, `--color-surface`, and `--color-text`. They are for things that are not intent-colored, such as a container's border, a dialog's background, and its text.

## Component variables

Eighteen variables are read by a single component and are supported inputs. A component reads each one where it is drawn, so a value set on the component or on any element around it reaches it, and the nearest value wins: set `--switch-width` on a form and every switch in it takes it. Every other variable a component declares, such as `--surface-padding` or any name that starts with `--_`, is internal and may change in any release.

| Variable               | Element        | Value                        | Default                                                                 | Effect                                                                                                |
| ---------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--progress-value`     | `.progress`    | A percentage, `0%` to `100%` | `0%`                                                                    | Width of the filled part. Not clamped; a value without `%` is invalid and shows empty.                |
| `--progress-color`     | `.progress`    | A color                      | The intent color                                                        | Color of the filled part and of the `.active` shimmer.                                                |
| `--progress-surface`   | `.progress`    | A color                      | The intent color at the presentation's fill: 12% by default             | Color of the track.                                                                                   |
| `--progress-edge`      | `.progress`    | A color                      | The intent's border color at the presentation's border: none by default | Color of the track's border. It shows only where the track has a border width, such as with `.edged`. |
| `--input-group-gap`    | `.input-group` | A length                     | `0.5rem`                                                                | Space between the control and its icon or text.                                                       |
| `--input-group-pad`    | `.input-group` | A length                     | `0.75rem`; `0.625rem` with `.sm` and `1rem` with `.lg`                  | Space between the group's edge and its content, on both sides.                                        |
| `--field-gap`          | `.field`       | A length                     | `0.35rem`                                                               | Space between a field's label, control, and hint.                                                     |
| `--switch-width`       | `.switch`      | A length                     | `2.5rem`                                                                | Width of the track. The knob keeps its size and travels further.                                      |
| `--switch-height`      | `.switch`      | A length                     | `1.25rem`                                                               | Height of the track. The knob grows with it.                                                          |
| `--tooltip-gap`        | `.tooltip`     | A length                     | `0.5rem`                                                                | Space between the trigger and the bubble.                                                             |
| `--tooltip-linger`     | `.tooltip`     | A time                       | `300ms`                                                                 | How long the bubble stays after the pointer leaves the trigger.                                       |
| `--divider-color`      | `.divider`     | A color                      | The intent color                                                        | Color of the line. It wins over an intent class on the divider.                                       |
| `--divider-width`      | `.divider`     | A length                     | The border width: `1px` by default                                      | Thickness of the line.                                                                                |
| `--skeleton-base`      | `.skeleton`    | A color                      | A faint tint of the intent color                                        | Color the placeholder rests on.                                                                       |
| `--skeleton-sheen`     | `.skeleton`    | A color                      | A stronger tint of the intent color                                     | Color of the highlight that sweeps across it.                                                         |
| `--quote-width`        | `.quote`       | A length                     | Twice the border width plus `1px`: `3px` by default                     | Thickness of the bar on the quotation's starting edge.                                                |
| `--table-cell-padding` | `.data-table`  | A `padding` value            | `0.75rem 1rem`                                                          | Padding of every header, body, and footer cell. A padding utility on a cell still wins.               |
| `--table-hover`        | `.data-table`  | A color                      | A 12% step toward the intent's hover color                              | Background of a body row under the pointer. `transparent` turns it off.                               |

```html
<div class="progress" role="meter" aria-label="Storage used" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="100" aria-valuenow="92" style="--progress-value: 92%; --progress-color: var(--color-warning)"></div>

<div class="input-group" style="--input-group-gap: 0">
  <span>app.example.com/u/</span>
  <input class="ipt" id="profile-url" aria-label="Profile address" />
</div>
```

The examples in context are in [Feedback → Show progress](docs/usage/feedback.md#show-progress), [Forms → Add an icon or a fixed prefix](docs/usage/forms.md#add-an-icon-or-a-fixed-prefix), and [Tooltips → Hover, linger, and Escape](docs/usage/tooltips.md#hover-linger-and-escape).

## Composition helpers

To build a component the package does not ship, such as a segmented control or a filter chip, compose it from the same classes the package's components are built from. With compiled CSS, write them as classes; with Tailwind source, you can also `@apply` them, together with the intent, presentation, elevation, and corner classes, which are utilities on `/tw` too: `@apply box box-hover neutral soft edgeless`. To give a shipped component a fixed recipe instead, such as a small soft primary button, see [Tailwind CSS v4 → Build your own components with `@apply`](docs/integrating/tailwind.md#build-your-own-components-with-apply).

| Class          | What it gives an element                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `box`          | The painted box: background, text color, border, corner, shadow, the aesthetic's material, the focus ring, and the disabled look. It reads intent, presentation, aesthetic, and elevation. |
| `box-hover`    | The hover color, for something pressed rather than typed into. Add it with `box`.                                                                                                          |
| `box-active`   | The press: a slight shrink, or the aesthetic's own press. Add it with `box`.                                                                                                               |
| `surface`      | `box` with a surface's defaults: no fill and a border, the surface corner, and the aesthetic's surface background, blur, and shadow, as on a card.                                         |
| `text-control` | `box` with a text field's defaults: no fill and a border, the capped fill and border rules, placeholder color, a border that changes on hover and focus, and the invalid state.            |

Filter chips for the members list, one pressed and one not:

```html
<button class="box box-hover box-active neutral soft edgeless" type="button" aria-pressed="true" style="padding: 0.25rem 0.75rem; border-radius: 999px">Admins</button>

<button class="box box-hover box-active neutral ghost edgeless" type="button" aria-pressed="false" style="padding: 0.25rem 0.75rem; border-radius: 999px">Owners</button>
```

`box` does not read `aria-pressed`, so the pressed chip looks pressed only because it has `.soft`. When your code changes `aria-pressed`, change the presentation class with it: `.soft` when pressed, `.ghost` when not.

What to give each one:

- **`box` needs a fill and an edge class.** It has no defaults of its own, so with no `.solid`, `.soft`, or `.ghost` and no `.edged` or `.edgeless`, on the element or a container, it draws nothing. `surface` and `text-control` have defaults and work alone.
- **Name the intent on `box`.** A `box` element takes the intent of the nearest element around it that has one, unlike the package's components. Put `.neutral` or an intent class on it. `surface` and `text-control` are neutral unless the element has an intent class, as components are.
- **`@apply` carries the whole helper.** `@utility my-field { @apply text-control; }` gets what `class="text-control"` gets: the neutral intent and the field border, `.soft`, `.solid`, and `.edgeless` on the element, and the invalid look for `aria-invalid="true"`. `@apply surface` is neutral the same way. An intent class you defined yourself must be plain CSS or a utility to color such an element, not a rule in `@layer components`.
- **Write the class that applies a helper as a utility.** What `@apply` copies lands in the [cascade layer](docs/setup.md#cascade-layers) of the rule it is written in. The helpers are utilities, and `@utility my-field` keeps your class in `utilities` beside them, so your other utilities still reach it. Written as plain CSS, `.my-field { @apply text-control; }` is unlayered, and everything the helper declares beats every utility on the element: an intent class you wrote as a utility leaves the field neutral, and `mt-8` does not move a dialog. Your own unlayered CSS still contests it, by specificity and then source order, as any two unlayered rules do.
- **A dialog works with `@apply surface`.** A closed `<dialog>` with your own `@apply surface` class stays hidden, and an open one is centered, as with `.card`. Hiding a closed one wins over a display utility such as `flex`; a margin you set still places an open one, and a margin utility does when your class is a utility too.
- **Size and spacing are yours.** None of the helpers sets padding, width, or height; `text-control` does not set the 2.5rem height that `.ipt` adds.
- **So are behavior and semantics.** Use a real `<button>`, `<input>`, or `<a href>`, or add the role and keyboard handling yourself, and set states such as `aria-pressed` or `aria-invalid`. `box` draws the disabled look for `disabled`, `.disabled`, `aria-disabled="true"`, and `data-disabled`, but only the `disabled` attribute stops input.

Do not set or read the `--_`-prefixed variables these helpers use internally; they change between releases.

## Next

[Content and layout](docs/usage/content-and-layout.md) lists the layout helpers, the type scale, surfaces, tables, and content chips.

<!-- Source: docs/usage/content-and-layout.md -->

# Content and layout

This is a lookup page for the classes that arrange a page and set its content: layout helpers, the type scale, cards and panels, tables, and the small content chips. [Building a screen](docs/concepts.md#lay-out-the-page) shows them in use.

## Layout

Every layout helper's gap is `--layout-gap`, `1rem` by default. Setting `--layout-gap` on an element changes the gap of every layout inside it. `.tight` and `.loose` change only the layout they are on; a layout nested inside keeps its own gap.

| Class              | Layout                                                                                                         | Gap                                              |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `.stack`           | A vertical column.                                                                                             | `--layout-gap`, `.tight` 0.5rem, `.loose` 1.5rem |
| `.cluster`         | A row that wraps, with items centered vertically. `.between` spreads the items to both ends.                   | Same                                             |
| `.view`            | A flex container. `.vertical` makes it a column; `.horizontal` a wrapping row with items centered.             | Same                                             |
| `.auto-grid`       | A grid of equal columns, each at least `--layout-grid-min` (16rem) wide, as many as fit.                       | Same                                             |
| `.section`         | Padding around a page section: `--layout-gutter` at the sides, `--layout-section-block` at the top and bottom. | None                                             |
| `.section-content` | Centers its content at a width of `--container-max` (80rem). `.narrow` uses 48rem, `.wide` 90rem.              | None                                             |
| `.divider`         | A horizontal line, as wide as its container. `.vertical` makes it a vertical line as tall as the row.          | None                                             |
| `.visually-hidden` | Hides content on screen and keeps it for screen readers.                                                       | None                                             |

`.auto-grid` fits two 16rem columns once its container is 32rem plus the gap wide, three at 48rem plus two gaps, and so on. Below one column's width, the column shrinks to fit. Set `--layout-grid-min` on the grid to change the column width.

`--layout-gutter` is `clamp(1rem, 4vw, 2rem)` and `--layout-section-block` is `clamp(4rem, 9vw, 7rem)`: both grow with the window between those bounds. The full list of foundation tokens is in [Theming → Foundation tokens](docs/usage/theming.md#foundation-tokens).

A `.divider` takes an intent, which colors it, and ignores presentation classes, so a `.ghost.edgeless` container does not hide the dividers inside it. Its width is the aesthetic's border width.

`.visually-hidden` is not named `.sr-only` because Tailwind ships a `.sr-only` of its own, and two classes with one name would conflict.

## Typography

| Class            | Size                          | Weight   | Letter spacing |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------- | -------- | -------------- |
| `.text-display`  | 3.75rem, 6rem from 48rem wide | Bold     | Tight          |
| `.text-title-lg` | 3rem, 3.75rem from 48rem wide | Bold     | Tight          |
| `.text-title`    | 1.875rem                      | Bold     | Tight          |
| `.text-title-sm` | 1.25rem                       | Semibold | Tight          |
| `.text-label-lg` | 1.125rem                      | Medium   | Wide           |
| `.text-label`    | 1rem                          | Medium   | Wide           |
| `.text-body`     | 0.875rem                      | Normal   | Wider          |

The two largest sizes grow at Tailwind's `md` breakpoint, 48rem by default. With the Tailwind source entrypoints, your own `md` breakpoint applies. The package sets no size on unclassed text: body text and unclassed headings take the browser's size, or the surrounding text size under the reset; see [Setup → Classless HTML](docs/setup.md#classless-html) for the classless mapping.

`.text-body` is 0.875rem, smaller than the 1rem page text; use it for secondary or dense copy, not for the page's main text. `/native` is the exception: it sets `.text-body` on `body`, so there it is the page text, and paragraphs and list items inherit it from whatever they sit in. See [Classless HTML](docs/setup.md#classless-html).

`.selection-contrast` on an element swaps the colors of selected text inside it to `--color-primary` on `--color-primary-contrast`. Use it on a `.solid.primary` area, where the default selection color would match the background.

## Surfaces

`.card` and `.panel` are the two containers. Both take intent, [presentation](docs/usage/composing.md#presentation), and [material tokens](docs/usage/customizing.md#material-tokens).

| Class    | Default look                                                                | Padding by default |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| `.card`  | No fill, a border, the surface corner, and a resting elevation of 1.        | 1.25rem            |
| `.panel` | The quiet background tone, no border, the surface corner, and no elevation. | 1rem               |

A resting elevation of 1 shows no shadow by itself. A card has a shadow only under an [aesthetic](docs/usage/aesthetics.md) that draws depth, or with `.raised` or `.floating`; see [Composing → Elevation](docs/usage/composing.md#elevation).

Padding classes:

| Class    | On `.card` | On `.panel` |
| -------- | ---------- | ----------- |
| `.p-xs`  | 0.5rem     | 0.25rem     |
| `.p-sm`  | 0.75rem    | 0.5rem      |
| _none_   | 1.25rem    | 1rem        |
| `.p-lg`  | 2rem       | 1.5rem      |
| `.flush` | 0          | 0           |

`.flush` is for content that runs edge to edge, such as an image or a table inside a card.

A padding class applies only to the card or panel it is on. A card or panel nested inside keeps its own padding, so a `.card.flush` holding a `.panel` still pads the panel by 1rem.

A panel is for sidebars, toolbars, and wells: areas that are part of the page, not objects on it. A card is a self-contained object, such as the profile card or the plan card on the settings screen.

### Neutral cards and panels

A neutral `.card.soft` and a neutral `.panel` show no tint: they rest on the quiet background tone one step off the page, so they read as a separate area without drawing attention. With a built-in intent they take the ordinary tint. [Composing → Neutral surfaces rest untinted](docs/usage/composing.md#neutral-surfaces-rest-untinted) has the details, including hover.

### Clickable cards

| Class          | Effect                                                                                                    |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.interactive` | Pointer cursor, hover color, press, and a focus ring. The same as `.hoverable` and `.pressable` together. |
| `.hoverable`   | The hover color only, with no pointer cursor.                                                             |
| `.pressable`   | The press and the pointer cursor only.                                                                    |

On the default look, a press scales the card down slightly (`scale(0.97)`); an aesthetic can replace that with its own press, and under a reduced-motion preference it still happens, at once.

Use one half for a card that answers only one gesture. A card that holds its own button takes `.hoverable`, so that pressing the button does not press the whole card.

```html
<article class="card">Neutral card</article>
<article class="card success solid">Filled success card</article>
<article class="card primary ghost edged">Intent border, no fill</article>
<a class="card success soft interactive" href="/settings/billing">Billing: tinted at rest, deeper on hover</a>
<article class="card hoverable">Tinted on hover; the action is a nested button</article>
<aside class="panel">A sidebar</aside>
```

These classes only style. Put them on a real link or button and give it an accessible name; a `<div class="card interactive">` cannot be focused or used from a keyboard.

A disabled `.interactive` or `.pressable` card shows the not-allowed cursor instead of the pointer, whether it is a `<button>` with `disabled`, or carries `.disabled`, `aria-disabled="true"`, or `data-disabled`.

## Tables

The settings screen lists API keys in a table:

```html
<div class="table-wrap">
  <table class="data-table">
    <caption class="visually-hidden">
      API keys
    </caption>
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th scope="col">Name</th>
        <th scope="col">Created</th>
        <th scope="col">Status</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr>
        <td>Deploy bot</td>
        <td>3 March 2026</td>
        <td>Active</td>
      </tr>
      <tr class="destructive">
        <td>Old laptop</td>
        <td>12 June 2024</td>
        <td>Revoked</td>
      </tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</div>
```

| Class         | Effect                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.data-table` | Styles a `<table>`: full width, `.text-body` text, a header background, the surface corner, cell padding, and a hover color on body rows. |
| `.table-wrap` | Scrolls a table sideways when it is wider than its container.                                                                             |
| `.ruled`      | On `.data-table`. Draws a line between body rows.                                                                                         |
| `.ruleless`   | On `.data-table`. Draws no lines inside the table.                                                                                        |

### Row intent

A table's rows take the table's intent, so `.data-table.success` colors its header and lines green. A row with its own intent class uses that instead, as the revoked key's `<tr class="destructive">` does. `<tr class="neutral">` sets a row back to neutral inside a colored table. On a `.solid` table, a row with its own intent keeps the table's text color so it stays readable on the table's fill, and shows its intent through its row line and hover. This is the one place an intent passes down, because rows are parts of the table, not separate components.

Only the six built-in intents and `.neutral` recolor a body row. A row with an intent you defined yourself, such as `<tr class="beta">`, looks like the rest of the table: its text, line, and hover come from the table's intent. To mark such a row, write a built-in intent class on the row and retheme that intent's color family on the row, as [Theming → Your own intent](docs/usage/theming.md#your-own-intent) describes, or paint the row with your own utilities.

### Table rules

A table draws lines under its header and above its footer. `.ruled` and `.ruleless` change them together with the lines between body rows:

| Class       | Under the header and above the footer | Between body rows |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `.ruleless` | No                                    | No                |
| _none_      | Yes                                   | No                |
| `.ruled`    | Yes                                   | Yes               |

`--ui-rule` is the token behind both classes, so a container can rule every table inside it: `style="--ui-rule: 100%"` acts like `.ruled`, and `0%` like `.ruleless`.

Three variables tune the rest, on the table or on any element around it. `--table-cell-padding` sets the padding of every cell, so `--table-cell-padding: 0.375rem 0.75rem` makes a dense table. `--table-hover` sets the color of a hovered body row, and `transparent` turns the hover off. `--ui-rule-ink` sets the color of a neutral table's lines; a table with an intent draws them in the intent's color. See [Customizing → Component variables](docs/usage/customizing.md#component-variables).

The frame around the table is separate: a table has no border by default, and `.edged` adds one. The three choices do not affect each other, so `.data-table.ruleless.edged` is a framed table with no lines inside, and `.data-table.ruled` has every row separated and no frame.

### Presentation on tables

A table reads [presentation](docs/usage/composing.md#presentation) on its header, its lines, and its border:

```html
<table class="data-table success soft edged">
  …
</table>
<table class="data-table ghost">
  <!-- No header background: only lines and text -->
</table>
```

- `.soft`, the default, gives the header the quiet background tone, `--color-foreground`, for every intent. A table has no hover state for a tint, so a `.data-table.success.soft` does not turn green; its lines and border do.
- `.ghost` removes the header background, leaving lines and text.
- `.solid` fills the header with the intent color.

### Corners and scrolling

A table takes the surface corner, like a card beside it. The corner cells carry the corners, so a `<caption>` above the table is not cut off in any browser. A cell that spans rows down into a bottom corner leaves that corner square.

`.table-wrap` scrolls, and a scrolling element cuts off whatever is drawn outside it, including a tooltip on a cell; see [Tooltips → Where a tooltip gets cut off](docs/usage/tooltips.md#where-a-tooltip-gets-cut-off).

- Under an aesthetic that draws a glow around components, such as `.cyber`, the wrapper makes room for the glow so it is not cut off. The wrapper then extends that far past its parent, which only shows when the parent touches the edge of the window.
- The wrapper can only make room for a glow from an aesthetic around it. Put the aesthetic class on `.table-wrap` or an element above it, not on the table alone.
- Shadows, such as a `.raised` table's, get no room and are cut off.

Keep the wrapper on any table that could be wider than its container; without it, a wide table widens the whole page.

## Quotes, code, and keys

| Class           | Use                                                                            | Default look                  | Intent colors            |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `.quote`        | A `<blockquote>`. A `<cite>` inside it is upright and takes the quote's color. | A bar at the start, no fill   | Bar, background, text    |
| `.quote-inline` | An inline `<q>` quotation.                                                     | Quotation styling only        | Nothing                  |
| `.kbd`          | A key the user presses, such as <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>.                               | A tinted chip with a border   | Background, border, text |
| `.code`         | Inline code.                                                                   | A tinted chip with no border  | Background, text         |
| `.pre`          | A block of code. It scrolls sideways when a line is too long.                  | A tinted block with no border | Background, text         |

```html
<p>Press <kbd class="kbd">Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd class="kbd">K</kbd> to search members.</p>
<p>Use the <code class="code">Authorization</code> header with your API key.</p>
<kbd class="kbd primary solid">Ctrl</kbd>
<kbd class="kbd primary soft edged">Shift</kbd>
```

A `.kbd`, `.code`, or `.pre` rests on its intent's subtle tone, `--color-surface` for neutral, and a built-in intent class adds 12% of its color over it. `.ghost` is not supported on these three: the tinted background is what makes them chips, so they keep it and `.ghost` changes nothing. Their font is `--font-mono`; see [Theming → Fonts](docs/usage/theming.md#fonts).

## Next

[Presets](docs/usage/presets.md) shows how to set a look once instead of on every element. [Accessibility](docs/accessibility.md) lists what the CSS does for your users and what your application still owes them.

<!-- Source: docs/usage/presets.md -->

# Presets

By now the settings screen says `btn primary soft sm` in a dozen places, and changing your mind means changing a dozen places. This page covers the three ways to set a look once: axis classes on a container, theme and material tokens, and your own component classes built with `@apply`. Each fits a different kind of "once".

## Which one to use

| You want                                                              | Reach for                                                   |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| Every component in one region to share a fill, an edge, or a material | [Axis classes on a container](#axis-classes-on-a-container) |
| Different colors, corners, borders, or depth for a page or a region   | [Theme and material tokens](#theme-and-material-tokens)     |
| One name for a recipe you repeat, such as "the save button"           | [Your own component classes](#your-own-component-classes)   |

They combine. A region can set a material token, sit under an aesthetic, and hold your own button class, and each element can still override what it inherits.

## Axis classes on a container

Some classes work on a container as well as on a component, and everything inside takes them:

- The presentation classes: `.solid`, `.soft`, `.ghost`, `.edged`, and `.edgeless`.
- The corner patterns: `.cut-diagonal` and `.cut-diagonal-reverse`.
- The [aesthetics](docs/usage/aesthetics.md), such as `.glass` or `.pixel`.

```html
<div class="cluster soft edged">
  <button class="btn primary" type="button">Bold</button>
  <button class="btn" type="button">Italic</button>
  <button class="btn destructive solid" type="button">Clear formatting</button>
</div>
```

The toolbar's buttons are soft and edged, and the last one asks for its own fill. A class on the element always beats one from a container.

The other axes do not pass down. Intent, elevation (`.flat`, `.raised`, `.floating`), and size (`.sm`, `.lg`) change only the element they are on, so a `.sm` toolbar does not shrink its buttons; [Composing → Combining classes](docs/usage/composing.md#combining-classes) explains why. An aesthetic class also sets its own corner pattern on its region, so a `.cut-diagonal` above a `.pixel` region does not reach inside it.

Use a container class when the look belongs to the region, such as a quiet sidebar, rather than to the components in it.

## Theme and material tokens

Tokens are CSS custom properties. Set one on `:root` and the whole page follows; set it on an element and only what is inside follows. They reach further than classes, because components read them while they draw:

```css
.admin {
  --radius-control: 0.25rem;
  --radius-surface: 0.5rem;
  --border-width: 2px;
}
```

Every button, field, tooltip bubble, and surface inside `.admin` takes the tighter corners and the heavier border, with no class on any of them. Checkboxes, `.kbd`, and `.code` keep their own smaller corner, `--radius-small`.

The tables live where the tokens are explained, so this page does not repeat them:

- [Theming → Color tokens](docs/usage/theming.md#color-tokens): brand and status colors, in both themes.
- [Theming → Foundation tokens](docs/usage/theming.md#foundation-tokens): corners, border width, control height, focus ring, depth, and motion.
- [Customizing → Presentation tokens](docs/usage/customizing.md#presentation-tokens): how much a fill, an edge, or a hover gives.
- [Customizing → Material tokens](docs/usage/customizing.md#material-tokens): what an aesthetic sets, which you can set yourself, such as `--ui-radius`.
- [Customizing → Aesthetic tokens](docs/usage/customizing.md#aesthetic-tokens): the knobs of each aesthetic, such as `--neo-offset`.

Use tokens when the change is a value, such as a color or a corner, rather than a choice between classes.

## Your own component classes

With the Tailwind source entrypoints, every component, helper, and axis class is a Tailwind utility, so one class of yours can carry the whole recipe:

```css
@import "@codenhub/styles/tw";

@utility btn-save {
  @apply btn primary soft sm;
}
```

```html
<button class="btn-save" type="submit">Save changes</button>
```

`btn-save` behaves like `btn primary soft sm` written out, aesthetics and hover included, and changing the recipe changes every save button. Modifiers that belong to one component, such as `.tight` on `.stack` or `.icon` on `.btn`, are utilities too, so `@apply btn icon` gives you an icon button of your own. [Tailwind CSS v4 → Build your own components with `@apply`](docs/integrating/tailwind.md#build-your-own-components-with-apply) has the rules, including why `@utility` beats a plain rule.

With the compiled CSS there is no `@apply`. Keep the recipe in one place on the other side instead: a template partial, a component in your framework, or a constant such as `const saveButton = "btn primary soft sm"`.

Use your own class when the same combination names one thing in your design, such as the save button or the plan card.

## Next

[Accessibility](docs/accessibility.md) lists what the CSS does for your users and what your application still owes them.

<!-- Source: docs/accessibility.md -->

# Accessibility

The settings screen is built, and the CSS has done its part along the way: every field shows where focus is, an invalid email turns red, and the spinner stops for users who ask for less motion. The rest is up to your HTML and JavaScript. This package styles states; it does not provide semantic elements, ARIA attributes, keyboard behavior, focus management, validation, or the timing of announcements.

This page lists both halves: what the CSS provides, and what your application has to add.

## Provided by CSS

### Focus and state

| Feature            | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `:focus-visible`   | A focus outline on every element, drawn with `--focus-ring`, `--focus-ring-width`, and `--focus-ring-offset`. On a component filled past half strength, such as a `.solid.primary` button, a 2px line of the page color runs inside the ring, so the ring stays visible on a fill of its own color.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Form control focus | `.ipt`, `.textarea`, and `.select` draw the focus outline and change their border to the intent color. Typed text in a field with an intent class is in the intent's readable tone, `--intent-strong`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Invalid controls   | `aria-invalid="true"` on a form control turns its border, focus color, and typed text destructive, the text in the destructive readable tone. A checkbox, radio, or switch is drawn exactly as its `.destructive` version, checked mark included.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Disabled controls  | `disabled`, `aria-disabled="true"`, `data-disabled`, and `.disabled` show the disabled cursor and opacity, and a disabled control does not react to hover, including inside an `.input-group`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Open state         | `data-state="open"` on a `.tooltip` shows its bubble without hover or focus, and `data-state="closed"` hides it while hovered or focused. No other component reads either.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Native `<dialog>`  | A `<dialog>` with `.card`, `.panel`, `.surface`, or your own class that does `@apply surface` stays hidden until it is opened, and opens centered. A margin you set on the dialog, as a utility or in your own CSS, still overrides the centering, except that a margin utility does not when your class applies `surface` in plain CSS; see [Customizing → Composition helpers](docs/usage/customizing.md#composition-helpers). With the [classless stylesheet](docs/setup.md#classless-html), a plain `<dialog>` is a `.card.floating` and behaves the same; with the other entrypoints, a dialog with none of these classes is left alone. Trapping focus, closing on Escape, and making the page behind it inert are up to your application. |

### Visually hidden content

`.visually-hidden` hides content on screen and keeps it for screen readers, as the API keys table's `<caption>` does in [Content and layout → Tables](docs/usage/content-and-layout.md#tables). It ships with the layout utilities: in `.`, `./native`, `./tw`, `./tw/native`, and `./tw/utilities`. It is not in `./components` or the `./tw/components` and `./tw/*` component entrypoints.

### Control boundaries

WCAG 1.4.11 asks that the boundary of a control you need to see to use it measures at least 3:1 against what is next to it.

| Feature                      | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Text controls at rest        | A text control's border rests lighter than its intent's full border, below 3:1 by choice, so hover and focus have a stronger tone to change to. [Increased contrast](#increased-contrast) draws it whole.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Toggles                      | `.checkbox`, `.radio`, and `.switch` draw their full border, because the border is the only thing that shows an unchecked box. A `.switch` with its own `.edgeless` is the exception, below.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `.edgeless` from a container | Ignored by every text control and toggle: a container cannot remove the border of a field or toggle inside it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `.edgeless` on the control   | `.ipt`, `.textarea`, `.select`, and `.switch` drop their border and no longer meet 1.4.11 at rest. `.switch.ghost` keeps its border even then, because with no fill and no border nothing would show the track.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `.checkbox`, `.radio`        | Always draw their border, from a container or with their own `.edgeless`. `.edgeless` on them is not supported.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Progress track               | By choice, the filled part carries the value and the track is a quiet background. The default track, `.soft.edgeless`, measures about 1.1:1 to 1.3:1 against the page. The filled part measures at least 3:1 against that track for every intent except warning in light (about 2.7:1) and info in dark (about 2.9:1). Where the track itself must meet 1.4.11, use `.ghost.edged` with an intent class; see [Progress outlines](#progress-outlines) below. |

### Progress outlines

On a `.progress.ghost.edged`, the track is the page, and its outline and the filled part are both drawn in the intent's color. Measured against the page, with no aesthetic:

| Intent         | Light page | Dark page | Meets 3:1                                                                |
| -------------- | ---------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `.primary`     | 18.96:1    | 18.96:1   | Yes                                                                      |
| `.secondary`   | 7.47:1     | 7.63:1    | Yes                                                                      |
| `.success`     | 5.14:1     | 3.69:1    | Yes                                                                      |
| `.warning`     | 3.06:1     | 6.20:1    | Yes                                                                      |
| `.destructive` | 5.80:1     | 3.27:1    | Yes                                                                      |
| `.info`        | 6.17:1     | 3.07:1    | Yes                                                                      |
| No intent      | 2.48:1     | 1.91:1    | No: the outline fails, though the filled part, in the text color, passes |

With no intent class, the outline is the quiet border gray, `--color-border`. To make a neutral track meet 1.4.11, give the bar an intent class, or set `--progress-edge` to a stronger color, such as `var(--color-accent)`, which measures 7.47:1 on a light page and 7.63:1 on a dark one. Warning on a light page and info on a dark one clear 3:1 by a small margin, so measure again if you change those colors.

### Motion and transparency

| Feature                    | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Reduced motion, components | With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, every component stops its own transitions and animations: the skeleton and progress shimmer, the indeterminate bar, the tooltip, the toggle marks, and the press's motion. The press itself still happens, at once, on the default look and under every aesthetic and solo class, since it is the feedback that a click landed. |
| Reduced motion, whole page | The reset also shortens every other animation and transition on the page.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Reduced transparency       | With `prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce`, and in forced colors, `.glass`, `.glass-liquid`, and `.glass-solo` drop their blur and lens and become opaque.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

Each component's reduced-motion rule ships with the component, so every entrypoint that includes it respects reduced motion without the reset, including `@codenhub/styles/components`, `@codenhub/styles/tw/components`, and each `/tw/*` component entrypoint. The complete and native entrypoints add the reset's page-wide rule.

The reset's rule is `!important` inside the `base` layer, and a layered `!important` beats an unlayered one, so your own `!important` cannot turn an animation back on. To keep one running for users who ask for reduced motion, such as an upload spinner you consider essential, declare it `!important` in a layer ordered before `base`. The first `@layer` statement the browser reads sets the order, so yours goes before the package:

```css
@layer essential-motion, theme, base, components, utilities;
@import "@codenhub/styles";

@layer essential-motion {
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
    .upload-spinner {
      animation-duration: 1s !important;
      animation-iteration-count: infinite !important;
    }
  }
}
```

Respecting reduced motion is not the whole requirement. Motion that keeps going next to content, such as a shimmer left on a card after it has loaded, needs a way to stop it for every user; see [Feedback → Animation that keeps running](docs/usage/feedback.md#animation-that-keeps-running).

### Increased contrast

With `prefers-contrast: more`, the borders the package draws below 3:1 by choice are drawn at 3:1 or more against what is next to them, in both themes. Text, solid fills, and focus rings already meet their ratios and do not change. `prefers-contrast: less` is not read.

| Feature         | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Text controls   | `.ipt`, `.textarea`, `.select`, and `.input-group` rest at their full border, so hover and focus no longer change its tone. The focus ring is the same.                                                                                                           |
| Neutral borders | `--color-border` takes a heavier gray, `neutral-600` in light and `neutral-400` in dark, so a card's border, a divider, a table's rules, and a neutral button's or badge's border meet 3:1. If you set `--color-border` yourself, your color is kept; measure it. |
| Intent borders  | An intent's border takes its strong tone, `--color-<intent>-strong`, so `.edged` on a `.soft` `.alert`, `.panel`, `.badge`, `.kbd`, `.code`, or `.pre` meets 3:1 against both its fill and the page, for every intent.                                            |
| Progress track  | The track draws an outline in its border color, which meets 3:1 with or without an intent class. `.edgeless` on the bar or on a container still removes it.                                                                                                       |
| Glass           | `.glass`, `.glass-liquid`, and `.glass-solo` drop their blur and lens and become opaque, as with reduced transparency, and their white hairline becomes a gray border.                                                                                            |
| Chunky tile     | `.chunky-tile` draws tiles and surfaces in the heavier gray its controls use.                                                                                                                                                                                     |

What you remove stays removed: `.edgeless` on a control still drops its border, and a `.panel` still has none unless you add `.edged`.

### Color and contrast

The measurements below are for the shipped colors. Once you change a color token, measure your own pairs again; [Theming → Change the brand color](docs/usage/theming.md#change-the-brand-color) shows which pairs to check.

| Feature                 | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Filled labels           | Every intent's `.solid` label meets 4.5:1 (WCAG 1.4.3) as normal text, in both themes. The lowest is success, at 5.14:1.                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Warning text            | `--color-warning-contrast` is near-black, not the page color, because an amber dark enough to carry white text no longer looks amber.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Partial fills           | The contrast text color appears only on fills above half strength, so a text control's capped fill keeps the intent's own text color.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Intent color in dark    | In dark mode a `.soft` or `.ghost` label uses the `-300` shade of its intent, so it keeps its hue instead of turning white.                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Text on a filled parent | A neutral component that is not `.solid`, such as a badge in a `.btn.primary` or a ghost button in a `.card.solid.primary`, prints in its parent's text color instead of the page's, so it keeps the parent's contrast.                                                                                                                            |
| Print                   | A page prints in the light theme, and filled components print their background (`print-color-adjust: exact`), so contrast text never lands on blank paper. A `dark:` utility still applies in print; see [Theming → Printing](docs/usage/theming.md#printing).                                                                                        |
| Toggle marks            | A checked mark measures at least 3:1 against every fill its presentation can give it, in both themes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Soft fills with borders | `.edged` on a `.soft` `.alert`, `.panel`, `.badge`, `.kbd`, `.code`, or `.pre` draws a border that measures below 3:1 against the 12% fill for some intents, which ones depending on the theme. Measure the pair before relying on that border as a control's boundary. [Increased contrast](#increased-contrast) brings every one of them to 3:1. |

### Forced colors and direction

| Feature        | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Forced colors  | With `forced-colors: active`, borders, checked states, a `.select`'s chevron, and a progress bar's value stay visible, drawn in system colors, under every aesthetic. An aesthetic that draws its border as an inner shadow, such as `.pixel`, draws a real border instead. Glass becomes opaque, because forced colors keep a background's transparency. |
| Text direction | Under `dir="rtl"`, the quote bar, the alert icon, the progress fill, the vertical divider, the switch knob, table alignment, and a select's chevron all switch sides. No class is needed.                                                                                                                                                                 |

In forced colors, `.text-control`, `.ipt`, `.textarea`, `.select`, the toggles, and your own class that does `@apply text-control` show a 2px `Highlight` focus outline. Inside an `.input-group`, the group draws the field's ring and the control inside draws none, so a focused field shows one ring. The native entrypoint gives unclassed text inputs, selects, textareas, checkboxes, and radios the same outline.

Checkboxes, radios, and switches use the system colors `Canvas`, `CanvasText`, `Highlight`, and `HighlightText`, so checked and unchecked stay distinct: a checked toggle is filled with `Highlight` and its mark is `HighlightText`, on the classes and in the native entrypoint alike. Shape, size, and spacing do not change.

A `.progress` bar does the same: its filled part is `CanvasText` on a `Canvas` track with a `CanvasText` outline, whatever its intent or presentation, so a half-full bar does not read as an empty one. The `.active` shimmer is not drawn.

## Required outside CSS

Use the HTML element that matches what the component does, and add the behavior the CSS cannot.

| UI               | What your application adds                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Buttons          | `<button>` for actions and `<a href>` for navigation. An accessible name, such as `aria-label`, on every `.btn.icon`.                                                                                                                                   |
| Forms            | A `<label>` for each control, the right `type`, validation, and `aria-describedby` linking hints and errors. Keep hints and errors outside the `<label>`, and give a `.switch` `role="switch"`.                                                         |
| Alerts           | `role="status"` for a confirmation such as "Profile saved", or `role="alert"` for an error that needs attention now.                                                                                                                                    |
| Toasts           | A live region, a way to dismiss it, focus rules, and a pause on any timeout.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Tooltips         | A real `id` and `role="tooltip"` on the bubble, referenced from the trigger's `aria-describedby`. Dismissal on Escape by writing `data-state="closed"`; see [Tooltips](docs/usage/tooltips.md#hover-linger-and-escape). The bubble can already be hovered. |
| Progress         | A `<progress>` element, or `role="progressbar"` or `role="meter"` with ARIA values, when the value must be announced.                                                                                                                                   |
| Skeletons        | `aria-hidden="true"` on loading visuals, including a spinner you bring, and the loading state announced some other way when needed.                                                                                                                     |
| Ongoing motion   | A way to pause, stop, or hide motion that is not essential; see [Feedback → Animation that keeps running](docs/usage/feedback.md#animation-that-keeps-running).                                                                                            |
